passages.name: 2022 全国新高考Ⅰ卷 阅读C
passages.title: 养老院老人照料母鸡排解孤独
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 养老与公益
passages.summary: 当地一家慈善组织发起一个项目，让伦敦养老院的老人照料母鸡，以减少孤独感、增进老年人的身心健康；该项目还被用来帮助痴呆症患者，养老院工作人员反映药物使用量有所减少。参与的老人和养老院负责人都对项目表示欢迎。目前英格兰东北部地区已有700位老人在照料母鸡，这家慈善组织也获得了资金支持，要把项目推广到全国。

paras.en: The elderly residents (居民) in care homes in London are being given hens to look after to stop them feeling lonely.
paras.zh: 伦敦养老院的老年住户正陆续领到母鸡来照料，以免他们感到孤独。

w.m: adj. 年长的；上了年纪的
阻止……做某事；使……不再做某事

paras.en: The project was dreamed up by a local charity (慈善组织) to reduce loneliness and improve elderly people’s wellbeing.
paras.zh: 这个项目是当地一家慈善组织构想出来的，旨在减少老年人的孤独感，增进他们的身心健康。

paras.en: It is also being used to help patients suffering from dementia, a serious illness of the mind.
paras.zh: 该项目还用于帮助痴呆症患者——痴呆症是一种严重的心智疾病。

paras.en: Staff in care homes have reported a reduction in the use of medicine where hens are in use.
paras.zh: 养老院的工作人员反映，在用上了母鸡的地方，用药有所减少。

w.m: n. 全体员工；工作人员

paras.en: Among those taking part in the project is 80-year-old Ruth Xavier.
paras.zh: 参与这个项目的人当中，就有80岁的露丝·泽维尔。

paras.en: She said: “I used to keep hens when I was younger and had to prepare their breakfast each morning before I went to school.”
paras.zh: 她说：“我年轻时养过母鸡，每天早上上学前都得给它们准备早饭。”

paras.en: “I like the project a lot.
paras.zh: “我非常喜欢这个项目。

paras.en: I am down there in my wheelchair in the morning letting the hens out and down there again at night to see they’ve gone to bed.”
paras.zh: 早上我坐着轮椅下去把母鸡放出来，晚上再下去看看它们是不是已经回窝睡觉了。”

paras.en: “It’s good to have a different focus.
paras.zh: “有点别的事情可以上心，挺好的。

paras.en: People have been bringing their children in to see the hens and residents come and sit outside to watch them.
paras.zh: 一直有人带着孩子进来看母鸡，住户们也会到外面坐着看它们。

paras.en: I’m enjoying the creative activities, and it feels great to have done something useful.”
paras.zh: 我很喜欢这些创意活动，做了点有用的事，感觉真好。”

w.m: adj. 有创意的；创造性的

paras.en: There are now 700 elderly people looking after hens in 20 care homes in the North East, and the charity has been given financial support to roll it out countrywide.
paras.zh: 目前，英格兰东北部地区的20家养老院里有700位老人在照料母鸡，这家慈善组织也已获得资金支持，要把这一项目推广到全国。

paras.en: Wendy Wilson, extra care manager at 60 Penfold Street, one of the first to embark on the project, said: “Residents really welcome the idea of the project and the creative sessions.
paras.zh: 彭福尔德街60号是最早开展这一项目的养老院之一，那里的特别护理经理温迪·威尔逊说：“住户们非常欢迎这个项目的理念和那些创意活动课。

w.m: n. （从事某项活动的）一段时间；一节课

paras.en: We are looking forward to the benefits and fun the project can bring to people here.”
paras.zh: 我们期待这个项目能给这里的人们带来益处和乐趣。”

paras.en: Lynn Lewis, director of Notting Hill Pathways, said: “We are happy to be taking part in the project.
paras.zh: 诺丁山路径组织（Notting Hill Pathways）的负责人林恩·刘易斯说：“我们很高兴能参与这个项目。

paras.en: It will really help connect our residents through a shared interest and creative activities.”
paras.zh: 它会借助共同的兴趣和创意活动，切实帮助我们的住户彼此建立联系。”

passages.name: 2022 全国新高考Ⅰ卷 阅读D
passages.title: 饮食变化如何催生新语音
passages.genre: 说明文 · 语言与人类演化
passages.summary: 一项历时五年的研究表明，与饮食相关的人类咬合变化带来了新的语音，如今世界上一半的语言中都有这些语音。研究发现，远古成年人的上下门牙是对齐的，难以发出“f”“v”这类唇齿音；后来人类颌部变成覆咬合结构，这类音就更容易发出了，而这一咬合变化与新石器时代农业的发展有关。这项研究推翻了“人类出现时所有语音就已存在”的流行观点。

paras.en: Human speech contains more than 2,000 different sounds, from the common “m” and “a” to the rare clicks of some southern African languages.
paras.zh: 人类言语中包含2000多种不同的语音，从常见的“m”和“a”，到非洲南部一些语言中罕见的咂音。

w.m: n. 咂音（一种吸气发出的辅音）

paras.en: But why are certain sounds more common than others?
paras.zh: 但为什么某些语音比其他语音更常见呢？

paras.en: A ground-breaking, five-year study shows that diet-related changes in human bite led to new speech sounds that are now found in half the world’s languages.
paras.zh: 一项开创性的、为期五年的研究表明，与饮食相关的人类咬合变化带来了新的语音，如今世界上一半的语言中都有这些语音。

w.m: n. 咬合（上下牙齿的对合关系）

paras.en: More than 30 years ago, the scholar Charles Hockett noted that speech sounds called labiodentals, such as “f” and “v”, were more common in the languages of societies that ate softer foods.
paras.zh: 30多年前，学者查尔斯·霍凯特就注意到，在吃较软食物的社会里，语言中“f”“v”这类被称为唇齿音的语音更为常见。

paras.en: Now a team of researchers led by Damián Blasi at the University of Zurich, Switzerland, has found how and why this trend arose.
paras.zh: 如今，由瑞士苏黎世大学达米安·布拉西领导的一个研究团队，已经查明了这一趋势是如何出现、又为何出现的。

paras.en: They discovered that the upper and lower front teeth of ancient human adults were aligned (对齐), making it hard to produce labiodentals, which are formed by touching the lower lip to the upper teeth.
paras.zh: 他们发现，远古成年人的上下门牙是对齐的，因此很难发出唇齿音，而唇齿音要靠下唇接触上齿才能发出。

paras.en: Later, our jaws changed to an overbite structure (结构), making it easier to produce such sounds.
paras.zh: 后来，我们人类的颌部变成了覆咬合结构，这类音发起来就更容易了。

w.m: n. 覆咬合（上齿覆盖在下齿前方）

paras.en: The team showed that this change in bite was connected with the development of agriculture in the Neolithic period.
paras.zh: 研究团队证明，咬合的这一变化与新石器时代农业的发展有关。

paras.en: Food became easier to chew at this point.
paras.zh: 这时，食物变得更容易咀嚼了。

paras.en: The jawbone didn’t have to do as much work and so didn’t grow to be so large.
paras.zh: 颌骨不必再那么费力，因此也就没有长得那么大。

paras.en: Analyses of a language database also confirmed that there was a global change in the sound of world languages after the Neolithic age, with the use of “f” and “v” increasing remarkably during the last few thousand years.
paras.zh: 对一个语言数据库的分析也证实，新石器时代之后，世界语言的语音发生了全球性的变化：在过去几千年里，“f”和“v”的使用显著增多。

paras.en: These sounds are still not found in the languages of many hunter-gatherer people today.
paras.zh: 如今，在许多狩猎采集民族的语言中，仍然没有这些音。

paras.en: This research overturns the popular view that all human speech sounds were present when human beings evolved around 300,000 years ago.
paras.zh: 这项研究推翻了一种流行的观点：人类大约在30万年前进化形成时，所有语音就已经存在了。

paras.en: “The set of speech sounds we use has not necessarily remained stable since the appearance of human beings, but rather the huge variety of speech sounds that we find today is the product of a complex interplay of things like biological change and cultural evolution,” said Steven Moran, a member of the research team.
paras.zh: “自人类出现以来，我们所使用的这套语音并不一定一直保持稳定；相反，今天我们看到的种类繁多的语音，是生物变化和文化演化等因素复杂交互作用的产物。”研究团队成员史蒂文·莫兰说。

passages.name: 2022 全国新高考Ⅱ卷 阅读C
passages.title: 像治理酒驾一样治理分心驾驶
passages.genre: 说明文 · 社会与安全
passages.summary: 过去七年里，美国大多数州已禁止司机开车时发短信，但分心驾驶问题似乎仍在加剧，道路交通事故正急剧上升。为此，立法者和公共卫生专家希望像对待酒驾一样对待分心驾驶。纽约州立法者提议给警察配备一种叫 Textalyzer 的设备，在车祸现场检查司机的手机是否有违规使用记录；曾推动纽约州2001年手持设备禁令的奥尔蒂斯认为，这项法案若成为法律，人们会更害怕在开车时碰手机。

paras.en: Over the last seven years, most states have banned texting by drivers, and public service campaigns have tried a wide range of methods to persuade people to put down their phones when they are behind the wheel.
paras.zh: 过去七年里，大多数州都已禁止司机发短信，公益宣传活动也尝试了各种各样的方法，劝说人们开车时放下手机。

paras.en: Yet the problem, by just about any measure, appears to be getting worse.
paras.zh: 然而，几乎无论用什么标准衡量，这个问题似乎都在恶化。

paras.en: Americans are still texting while driving, as well as using social networks and taking photos.
paras.zh: 美国人仍然边开车边发短信，还会使用社交网络、拍照。

paras.en: Road accidents, which had fallen for years, are now rising sharply.
paras.zh: 道路交通事故此前多年一直在减少，如今正急剧上升。

paras.en: That is partly because people are driving more, but Mark Rosekind, the chief of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, said distracted (分心) driving was “only increasing, unfortunately.”
paras.zh: 这在一定程度上是因为人们开车开得更多了，但美国国家公路交通安全管理局局长马克·罗斯金德表示，分心驾驶“很遗憾，只增不减”。

w.m: adv. 部分地；在一定程度上
adv. 遗憾的是；不幸的是

paras.en: “Big change requires big ideas,” he said in a speech last month, referring broadly to the need to improve road safety.
paras.zh: “大变革需要大思路，”他上个月在一次演讲中说。这番话泛指道路安全有待改善。

paras.en: So to try to change a distinctly modern behavior, lawmakers and public health experts are reaching back to an old approach: They want to treat distracted driving like drunk driving.
paras.zh: 因此，为了设法改变一种明显带有现代特征的行为，立法者和公共卫生专家正回过头去借鉴一种老办法：他们想要像对待酒驾一样对待分心驾驶。

paras.en: An idea from lawmakers in New York is to give police officers a new device called the Textalyzer.
paras.zh: 纽约州立法者提出的一个想法是，给警察配备一种叫作 Textalyzer（“短信检测仪”）的新设备。

paras.en: It would work like this: An officer arriving at the scene of a crash could ask for the phones of the drivers and use the Textalyzer to check in the operating system for recent activity.
paras.zh: 设想中的用法是这样的：警察赶到车祸现场后，可以要求涉事司机交出手机，并用 Textalyzer 检查手机操作系统里最近的使用记录。

w.m: n. 活动；（设备的）使用情况

paras.en: The technology could determine whether a driver had just texted, emailed or done anything else that is not allowed under New York’s hands-free driving laws.
paras.zh: 这项技术能判定司机是否刚刚发过短信、电子邮件，或做过纽约州免提驾驶法律所不允许的其他任何事情。

paras.en: “We need something on the books that can change people’s behavior,” said Félix W. Ortiz, who pushed for the state’s 2001 ban on hand-held devices by drivers.
paras.zh: “我们需要一条能改变人们行为的法规，”费利克斯·W.奥尔蒂斯说。他曾推动纽约州在2001年出台法令，禁止司机使用手持设备。

w.m: （法律）已列入法典；已正式生效

paras.en: If the Textalyzer bill becomes law, he said, “people are going to be more afraid to put their hands on the cell phone.”
paras.zh: 他说，如果 Textalyzer 法案成为法律，“人们会更不敢碰手机”。

passages.name: 2022 全国新高考Ⅱ卷 阅读D
passages.title: 中年锻炼或可逆转心脏衰老
passages.genre: 说明文 · 健康与运动
passages.summary: 随着年龄增长，即使身体健康，心脏处理氧气的效率也会下降。得克萨斯大学的莱文博士让45至64岁、平时锻炼不多的健康志愿者参加研究，两年后，坚持高强度有氧运动的一组心脏健康显著改善，而参加低强度运动的一组心脏没有变化。莱文认为，中年后期是开始锻炼的最佳时机；美国心脏协会的戈德堡博士认为这些发现是一个很好的开端，但这项研究规模较小，还需要在大得多的人群中重复进行，以确定锻炼方案中究竟哪些方面作用最大。

paras.en: As we age, even if we’re healthy, the heart just isn’t as efficient in processing oxygen as it used to be.
paras.zh: 随着年龄增长，即使身体健康，心脏处理氧气的效率也不如从前了。

paras.en: In most people the first signs show up in their 50s or early 60s.
paras.zh: 对大多数人来说，最初的迹象在五十多岁或六十岁出头时出现。

w.m: adj. 初期的；（年龄段）前段的

paras.en: And among people who don’t exercise, the changes can start even sooner.
paras.zh: 而在不锻炼的人当中，这些变化甚至可能来得更早。

w.m: adv. 早；快（比较级 sooner：更早）

paras.en: “Think of a rubber band.
paras.zh: “想想橡皮筋吧。

paras.en: In the beginning, it is flexible, but put it in a drawer for 20 years and it will become dry and easily broken,” says Dr. Ben Levine, a heart specialist at the University of Texas.
paras.zh: 起初，它很有弹性，可要是把它放在抽屉里20年，它就会变得干燥、容易断裂，”得克萨斯大学的心脏病专家本·莱文博士说。

paras.en: That’s what happens to the heart.
paras.zh: 心脏的情况正是如此。

paras.en: Fortunately for those in midlife, Levine is finding that even if you haven’t been an enthusiastic exerciser, getting in shape now may help improve your aging heart.
paras.zh: 值得中年人庆幸的是，莱文的研究发现，即使你过去并不热衷于锻炼，现在开始健身也可能有助于改善你日渐衰老的心脏。

w.m: 健身；（通过锻炼）变得强健

paras.en: Levine and his research team selected volunteers aged between 45 and 64 who did not exercise much but were otherwise healthy.
paras.zh: 莱文和他的研究团队挑选了一批年龄在45到64岁之间的志愿者，他们平时锻炼不多，但其他方面都很健康。

paras.en: Participants were randomly divided into two groups.
paras.zh: 参与者被随机分成两组。

paras.en: The first group participated in a program of nonaerobic (无氧) exercise—balance training and weight training—three times a week.
paras.zh: 第一组参加了一项无氧运动计划，内容为平衡训练和力量训练，每周三次。

paras.en: The second group did high-intensity aerobic exercise under the guidance of a trainer for four or more days a week.
paras.zh: 第二组则在教练的指导下进行高强度有氧运动，每周四天或更多。

paras.en: After two years, the second group saw remarkable improvements in heart health.
paras.zh: 两年后，第二组的心脏健康状况有了显著改善。

paras.en: “We took these 50-year-old hearts and turned the clock back to 30- or 35-year-old hearts,” says Levine.
paras.zh: “我们让这些50岁的心脏时光倒流，变回了30或35岁的心脏，”莱文说。

paras.en: “And the reason they got so much stronger and fitter was that their hearts could now fill a lot better and pump (泵送) a lot more blood during exercise.”
paras.zh: “他们之所以变得强壮、健康得多，是因为他们的心脏现在充盈能力大大增强，在运动时也能泵出多得多的血液。”

paras.en: But the hearts of those who participated in less intense exercise didn’t change, he says.
paras.zh: 但他说，那些参加低强度运动的人，心脏没有发生变化。

paras.en: “The sweet spot in life to start exercising, if you haven’t already, is in late middle age when the heart still has flexibility,” Levine says.
paras.zh: “如果你还没有开始锻炼，那么人生中开始锻炼的最佳时机是中年后期，那时心脏仍有弹性，”莱文说。

paras.en: “We put healthy 70-year-olds through a yearlong exercise training program, and nothing happened to them at all.”
paras.zh: “我们让一些健康的70岁老人参加了为期一年的运动训练计划，结果他们身上什么变化都没有发生。”

paras.en: Dr. Nieca Goldberg, a spokeswoman for the American Heart Association, says Levine’s findings are a great start.
paras.zh: 美国心脏协会的女发言人妮卡·戈德堡博士说，莱文的研究发现是一个很好的开端。

paras.en: But the study was small and needs to be repeated with far larger groups of people to determine exactly which aspects of an exercise routine make the biggest difference.
paras.zh: 但这项研究规模较小，需要在规模大得多的人群中重复进行，以确定锻炼方案中究竟哪些方面作用最大。

w.m: n. 常规；固定的一套安排

passages.name: 2022 全国甲卷 阅读C
passages.title: 金妮独自远赴南极
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 人物与旅行
passages.summary: 金妮·巴兹林顿从小就热爱旅行。她曾是职业舞蹈演员，退休、儿子们也离家独立后，她开始周游世界，并在智利发现可以买到开往南极洲的临时廉价船票。2008年3月，她独自出行，与48位素不相识的乘客一同乘船前往南极洲，那里的野生动物、日出和座头鲸都令她难忘。她深切认识到，南极洲是一片应受到人类尊重的珍贵土地。

paras.en: As Ginni Bazlinton reached Antarctica, she found herself greeted by a group of little Gentoo penguins (企鹅) longing to say hello.
paras.zh: 金妮·巴兹林顿抵达南极洲时，迎接她的是一群急着跟她打招呼的小巴布亚企鹅。

w.m: 发现自己（处于某种境况）

paras.en: These gentle, lovely gatekeepers welcomed her and kick-started what was to be a trip Ginni would never forget.
paras.zh: 这些温顺可爱的“守门人”迎接了她，也由此开启了一段注定让金妮终生难忘的旅程。

paras.en: Ever since her childhood, Ginni, now 71, has had a deep love for travel.
paras.zh: 金妮如今71岁，从童年起就一直深爱旅行。

paras.en: Throughout her career (职业) as a professional dancer, she toured in the UK, but always longed to explore further.
paras.zh: 在整个职业舞蹈演员生涯中，她一直在英国各地巡演，但始终渴望去更远的地方探索。

paras.en: When she retired from dancing and her sons eventually flew the nest, she decided it was time to take the plunge.
paras.zh: 等她告别舞台、儿子们也终于离家独立后，她认定是时候勇敢迈出这一步了。

w.m: 毅然决定；勇敢迈出一步

paras.en: After taking a degree at Chichester University in Related Arts, Ginni began to travel the world, eventually getting work teaching English in Japan and Chile.
paras.zh: 在奇切斯特大学获得相关艺术专业学位后，金妮开始周游世界，后来在日本和智利找到了教英语的工作。

paras.en: And it was in Chile she discovered she could get last-minute cheap deals on ships going to Antarctica from the islands off Tierra del Fuego, the southernmost tip of South America.
paras.zh: 也正是在智利，她发现，从南美洲最南端火地岛附近的岛屿开往南极洲的船，临近开船时能买到便宜的特价票。

w.m: adj. 最后一刻的；临时的
prep. 在……附近海域；离……不远

paras.en: “I just decided I wanted to go,” she says.
paras.zh: “我就是打定主意要去，”她说。

paras.en: “I had no idea about what I’d find there and I wasn’t nervous, I just wanted to do it.
paras.zh: “我完全不知道会在那里看到什么，也不紧张，我就是想去做这件事。

paras.en: And I wanted to do it alone as I always prefer it that way.”
paras.zh: 而且我想独自去，因为我一向更喜欢那样。”

paras.en: In March 2008, Ginni boarded a ship with 48 passengers she’d never met before, to begin the journey towards Antarctica.
paras.zh: 2008年3月，金妮和48位素不相识的乘客一起登上一艘船，开始了前往南极洲的旅程。

paras.en: “From seeing the wildlife to witnessing sunrises, the whole experience was amazing.
paras.zh: “从观赏野生动物到亲眼看日出，整个经历都太棒了。

w.m: adj. 令人惊叹的；极好的

paras.en: Antarctica left an impression on me that no other place has,” Ginni says.
paras.zh: 南极洲给我留下的印象，是别的任何地方都不曾给过我的，”金妮说。

paras.en: “I remember the first time I saw a humpback whale; it just rose out of the water like some prehistoric creature and I thought it was smiling at us.
paras.zh: “我记得第一次看到座头鲸的情景；它就那样从水里浮了上来，像某种史前生物，我觉得它在对我们微笑。

paras.en: You could still hear the operatic sounds it was making underwater.”
paras.zh: 你还能听到它在水下发出的歌剧般的声音。”

paras.en: The realization that this is a precious land, to be respected by humans, was one of the biggest things that hit home to Ginni.
paras.zh: 意识到这是一片珍贵的土地，应当受到人类的尊重——这是让金妮感触最深的事情之一。

passages.name: 2022 全国甲卷 阅读D
passages.title: 悉尼：在现代与传统之间
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 城市与文化
passages.summary: 作者在悉尼随渡轮驾驶员安德鲁往返于港湾两岸，得知这些老渡轮将被双体船取代。该市的官方历史学家认为，悉尼在20世纪70年代急于实现现代化，抛弃了许多过去的东西，至今仍拿不定主意要做现代城市还是传统城市。一位年轻商人则认为，移民带来的古老文化加上年轻国家的干劲与活力，是一种难以超越的组合。作者认同他的看法，却仍忍不住希望保留那些老渡轮。

paras.en: Sometime in the early 1960s, a significant thing happened in Sydney, Australia.
paras.zh: 20世纪60年代初的某个时候，澳大利亚悉尼发生了一件意义重大的事。

w.m: adj. 重大的；意义深远的

paras.en: The city discovered its harbor.
paras.zh: 这座城市发现了自己的港湾。

paras.en: Then, one after another, Sydney discovered lots of things that were just sort of there — broad parks, superb beaches, and a culturally diverse population.
paras.zh: 接着，悉尼又接二连三地发现了许多似乎一直就在那儿的东西——宽阔的公园、绝佳的海滩，以及文化多元的居民。

paras.en: But it is the harbor that makes the city.
paras.zh: 但真正成就这座城市的，是它的港湾。

paras.en: Andrew Reynolds, a cheerful fellow in his early 30s, pilots Sydney ferryboats for a living.
paras.zh: 安德鲁·雷诺兹三十出头，是个乐呵呵的小伙子，以驾驶悉尼的渡轮为生。

paras.en: I spent the whole morning shuttling back and forth across the harbor with him.
paras.zh: 我跟着他在港湾两岸之间来回穿梭了一整个上午。

paras.en: After our third run Andrew shut down the engine, and we went our separate ways — he for a lunch break, I to explore the city.
paras.zh: 第三趟跑完后，安德鲁关掉了发动机，我们便各走各的——他去吃午饭、休息，我去游览这座城市。

paras.en: “I’ll miss these old boats,” he said as we parted.
paras.zh: “我会怀念这些老船的，”分别时他说。

paras.en: “How do you mean?”
paras.zh: “这话怎么讲？”

w.m: 你这话是什么意思；这话怎么讲

paras.en: I asked.
paras.zh: 我问道。

paras.en: “Oh, they’re replacing them with catamarans.
paras.zh: “哦，他们要用双体船来替换这些老船了。

paras.en: Catamarans are faster, but they’re not so elegant, and they’re not fun to pilot.
paras.zh: 双体船速度更快，但没那么优雅，开起来也没意思。

paras.en: But that’s progress, I guess.”
paras.zh: 不过，我想这就是进步吧。”

paras.en: Everywhere in Sydney these days, change and progress are the watchwords (口号), and traditions are increasingly rare.
paras.zh: 如今在悉尼，无论走到哪里，变革与进步都是人们的口号，传统则越来越少见了。

paras.en: Shirley Fitzgerald, the city’s official historian, told me that in its rush to modernity in the 1970s, Sydney swept aside much of its past, including many of its finest buildings.
paras.zh: 该市的官方历史学家雪莉·菲茨杰拉德告诉我，20世纪70年代，悉尼在急于实现现代化的过程中，抛弃了许多过去的东西，其中包括不少最精美的建筑。

paras.en: “Sydney is confused about itself,” she said.
paras.zh: “悉尼对自己的定位很困惑，”她说。

paras.en: “We can’t seem to make up our minds whether we want a modern city or a traditional one.
paras.zh: “我们似乎拿不定主意，到底想要一座现代城市还是一座传统城市。

paras.en: It’s a conflict that we aren’t getting any better at resolving (解决).”
paras.zh: 这是一个矛盾，而我们解决它的能力丝毫没有长进。”

paras.en: On the other hand, being young and old at the same time has its attractions.
paras.zh: 另一方面，既年轻又古老，也自有其魅力。

paras.en: I considered this when I met a thoughtful young businessman named Anthony.
paras.zh: 在结识一位名叫安东尼、颇有思想的年轻商人时，我想到了这一点。

w.m: adj. 有思想的；深思熟虑的

paras.en: “Many people say that we lack culture in this country,” he told me.
paras.zh: “很多人说我们这个国家缺乏文化，”他对我说。

paras.en: “What people forget is that the Italians, when they came to Australia, brought 2000 years of their culture, the Greeks some 3000 years, and the Chinese more still.
paras.zh: “人们忘记了，意大利人来到澳大利亚时，带来了他们2000年的文化，希腊人带来了大约3000年的文化，中国人带来的还要更多。

paras.en: We’ve got a foundation built on ancient cultures but with the drive and dynamism of a young country.
paras.zh: 我们的根基建立在古老文化之上，同时又有着一个年轻国家的干劲与活力。

paras.en: It’s a pretty hard combination to beat.”
paras.zh: 这样的组合，相当难以超越。”

paras.en: He is right, but I can’t help wishing they would keep those old ferries.
paras.zh: 他说得对，但我还是忍不住希望他们能保留那些老渡轮。

passages.name: 2022 全国乙卷 阅读C
passages.title: 无人机守护铁路安全
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与交通
passages.summary: 文章探讨用无人机检查铁路的前景：无人机已用于检查高压输电线，同样可以检查铁路线路以及铁轨、道岔等基础设施，有望提高铁路的安全性、可靠性和准点率，降低维护成本，并让维护人员免于危险作业。工程师们正在研发未来的铁路无人机，它们将在列车前方的轨道上自主运行，像副驾驶一样为列车引路，发现问题时发出信号，让列车及时作出反应。

paras.en: Can a small group of drones (无人机) guarantee the safety and reliability of railways and, at the same time, help railway operators save billions of euros each year?
paras.zh: 一小群无人机能否保障铁路的安全性和可靠性，同时帮助铁路运营商每年节省数十亿欧元？

paras.en: That is the very likely future of applying today’s “eyes in the sky” technology to making sure that the millions of kilometres of rail tracks and infrastructure (基础设施) worldwide are safe for trains on a 24/7 basis.
paras.zh: 这极有可能就是当今“空中之眼”技术未来的应用前景：用它来确保全球数百万公里的铁轨和基础设施全天候都能让列车安全通行。

w.m: 空中之眼（指空中监测技术）
全天候地（每天24小时、每周7天）

paras.en: Drones are already being used to examine high-tension electrical lines.
paras.zh: 无人机目前已被用于检查高压输电线。

paras.en: They could do precisely the same thing to inspect railway lines and other vital aspects of rail infrastructure such as the correct position of railway tracks and switching points.
paras.zh: 它们可以用完全相同的方式检查铁路线路以及铁路基础设施的其他重要方面，比如铁轨和道岔的位置是否正确。

paras.en: The more regularly the lines can be inspected, the more railway safety, reliability and on-time performance will be improved.
paras.zh: 线路检查得越频繁，铁路的安全性、可靠性和准点率就提高得越多。

paras.en: Costs would be cut and operations would be more efficient (高效) across the board.
paras.zh: 成本会降低，运营也会全面变得更加高效。

paras.en: That includes huge savings in maintenance costs and better protection of railway personnel.
paras.zh: 这包括大幅节省维护成本，以及更好地保护铁路工作人员。

paras.en: It is calculated that European railways alone spend approximately 20 billion euros a year on maintenance, including sending maintenance staff, often at night, to inspect and repair the rail infrastructure.
paras.zh: 据计算，仅欧洲的铁路每年就在维护上花费约200亿欧元，其中包括派遣维护人员去检查和维修铁路基础设施，而且常常是在夜间。

paras.en: That can be dangerous work that could be avoided with drones assisting the crews’ efforts.
paras.zh: 这类工作可能有危险，而如果有无人机协助工作人员作业，这类工作就可以避免。

w.m: n. 一组工作人员；作业队

paras.en: By using the latest technologies, drones could also start providing higher-value services for railways, detecting faults in the rail or switches, before they can cause any safety problems.
paras.zh: 借助最新技术，无人机还可以开始为铁路提供更高价值的服务，在铁轨或道岔的故障引发任何安全问题之前就把它们检测出来。

paras.en: To perform these tasks, drones for rail don’t need to be flying overhead.
paras.zh: 要完成这些任务，铁路无人机并不需要在空中飞行。

w.m: adv. 在头顶上方；在空中

paras.en: Engineers are now working on a new concept: the rail drones of the future.
paras.zh: 工程师们目前正在研究一个新概念：未来的铁路无人机。

paras.en: They will be moving on the track ahead of the train, and programmed to run autonomously.
paras.zh: 它们将在列车前方的轨道上行驶，并通过编程实现自主运行。

paras.en: Very small drones with advanced sensors and AI, travelling ahead of the train, could guide it like a co-pilot.
paras.zh: 配备先进传感器和人工智能的微型无人机在列车前方行进，可以像副驾驶一样为列车引路。

paras.en: With their ability to see ahead, they could signal any problem, so that fast-moving trains would be able to react in time.
paras.zh: 凭借察看前方的能力，它们一旦发现任何问题都能发出信号，让高速行驶的列车能够及时作出反应。

passages.name: 2022 全国乙卷 阅读D
passages.title: 软饮料糖税收入仅为预期一半
passages.genre: 新闻报道 · 健康与社会政策
passages.summary: 首批官方数据显示，政府对软饮料征收的糖税带来的收入只有大臣们最初预测的一半；此前，制造商为了避税，已降低了商店在售软饮料中一半以上产品的含糖量。不过，一些高糖品牌接受了糖税，拒绝做出改变。一位政府官员认为，糖税正在产生积极影响，为学校的体育设施和更健康的饮食筹集了数百万英镑。

paras.en: The Government’s sugar tax on soft drinks has brought in half as much money as Ministers first predicted it would generate, the first official data on the policy has shown.
paras.zh: 首批关于这项政策的官方数据显示，政府对软饮料征收的糖税带来的收入只有大臣们最初预测的一半。

paras.en: First announced in March 2016, the tax, which applies to soft drinks containing more than 5g of sugar per 100ml, was introduced to help reduce childhood obesity (肥胖).
paras.zh: 这项税于2016年3月首次宣布，适用于每100毫升含糖量超过5克的软饮料，其出台是为了帮助减少儿童肥胖。

paras.en: It is believed that today’s children and teenagers are consuming three times the recommended level of sugar, putting them at a higher risk of the disease.
paras.zh: 据信，如今的儿童和青少年摄入的糖是推荐量的三倍，这使他们患上这种疾病的风险更高。

paras.en: Initially the sugar tax was expected to make £520m a year for the Treasury.
paras.zh: 最初，糖税预计每年能为财政部带来5.2亿英镑收入。

paras.en: However, data from the first six months showed it would make less than half this amount.
paras.zh: 然而，前六个月的数据显示，糖税的收入将不到这一数额的一半。

paras.en: At present it is expected to generate £240m for the year ending in April 2019, which will go to school sports.
paras.zh: 目前，预计在截至2019年4月的这一年里，糖税将带来2.4亿英镑收入，这笔钱将用于学校体育。

paras.en: It comes after more than half of soft drinks sold in shops have had their sugar levels cut by manufacturers (制造商) so they can avoid paying the tax.
paras.zh: 此前，为了避免缴纳这项税，制造商已经降低了商店在售软饮料中一半以上产品的含糖量。

paras.en: Drinks now contain 45 million fewer kilos of sugar as a result of manufacturers’ efforts to avoid the charge, according to Treasury figures.
paras.zh: 根据财政部的数据，由于制造商努力规避这项税费，如今饮料中的糖减少了4500万千克。

paras.en: Since April, drinks companies have been forced to pay between 18p and 24p for every litre of sugary drink they produce or import, depending on the sugar content.
paras.zh: 自4月以来，饮料公司被迫为其生产或进口的每升含糖饮料缴纳18至24便士，具体金额取决于含糖量。

paras.en: However, some high-sugar brands, like Classic Coca-Cola, have accepted the sugar tax and are refusing to change for fear of upsetting consumers.
paras.zh: 然而，经典可口可乐等一些高糖品牌已经接受了糖税，并且唯恐惹得消费者不满而拒绝做出改变。

paras.en: Fruit juices, milk-based drinks and most alcoholic drinks are free of the tax, as are small companies manufacturing less than 1m litres per year.
paras.zh: 果汁、奶基饮料和大多数含酒精饮料都免征这项税，每年生产不足100万升饮料的小公司也是如此。

w.m: adj. 以奶为主要成分的

paras.en: Today’s figures, according to one government official, show the positive influence the sugar tax is having by raising millions of pounds for sports facilities (设施) and healthier eating in schools.
paras.zh: 据一位政府官员称，今天公布的数据表明，糖税正在产生积极影响，为学校的体育设施和更健康的饮食筹集了数百万英镑。

paras.en: Helping the next generation to have a healthy and active childhood is of great importance, and the industry is playing its part.
paras.zh: 帮助下一代度过健康而充满活力的童年非常重要，而饮料行业也在尽自己的一份力。

w.m: adj. 充满活力的；好动的；积极的

paras.en: “What would the world be if there were no hunger?”
It’s a question that Professor Crystal would ask her students.
They found it hard to answer, she wrote later, because imagining something that isn’t part of real life—and learning how to make it real—is a rare skill.
It is taught to artists and engineers, but much less often to scientists.
Crystal set out to change that, and helped to create a global movement.
The result—an approach known as systems thinking—is now seen as essential in meeting global challenges.

Systems thinking is crucial to achieving targets such as zero hunger and better nutrition because it requires considering the way in which food is produced, processed, delivered and consumed, and looking at how those things intersect (交叉) with human health, the environment, economics and society.
According to systems thinking, changing the food system—or any other network—requires three things to happen.

First, researchers need to identify all the players in that system; second, they must work out how they relate to each other; and third, they need to understand and quantify the impact of those relationships on each other and on those outside the system.
Take nutrition.
In the latest UN report on global food security, the number of undernourished (营养不良) people in the world has been rising, despite great advances in nutrition science.
Tracking of 150 biochemicals in food has been important in revealing the relationships between calories, sugar, fat and the occurrence of common diseases.
But using machine learning and artificial intelligence, some scientists propose that human diets consist of at least 26,000 biochemicals—and that the vast majority are not known.
This shows that we have some way to travel before achieving the first objective of systems thinking—which, in this example, is to identify more constituent parts of the nutrition system.
A systems approach to creating change is also built on the assumption that everyone in the system has equal power.
But as some researchers find, the food system is not an equal one.
A good way to redress (修正) such power imbalance is for more universities to do what Crystal did and teach students how to think using a systems approach.
More researchers, policymakers and representatives from the food industry must learn to look beyond their direct lines of responsibility and adopt a systems approach.
Crystal knew that visions alone don’t produce results, but concluded that “we’ll never produce results that we can’t envision”.
Quantum (量子) computers have been on my mind a lot lately.
A friend has been sending me articles on how quantum computers might help solve some of the biggest challenges we face as humans.
I’ve also had exchanges with two quantum-computing experts.
One is computer scientist Chris Johnson who I see as someone who helps keep the field honest.
The other is physicist Philip Taylor.
For decades, quantum computing has been little more than a laboratory curiosity.
Now, big tech companies have invested in quantum computing, as have many smaller ones.
According to Business Weekly, quantum machines could help us “cure cancer, and even take steps to turn climate change in the opposite direction.”
This is the sort of hype (炒作) that annoys Johnson.
He worries that researchers are making promises they can’t keep.
“What’s new,” Johnson wrote, “is that millions of dollars are now potentially available to quantum computing researchers.”
As quantum computing attracts more attention and funding, researchers may mislead investors, journalists, the public and, worst of all, themselves about their work’s potential.
If researchers can’t keep their promises, excitement might give way to doubt, disappointment and anger, Johnson warns.
Lots of other technologies have gone through stages of excitement.
But something about quantum computing makes it especially prone to hype, Johnson suggests, perhaps because “‘quantum’ stands for something cool you shouldn’t be able to understand.”
And that brings me back to Taylor, who suggested that I read his book Q for Quantum.
After I read the book, Taylor patiently answered my questions about it.
He also answered my questions about PyQuantum, the firm he co-founded in 2016.
Taylor shares Johnson’s concerns about hype, but he says those concerns do not apply to PyQuantum.

The company, he says, is closer than any other firm “by a very large margin (幅度)” to building a “useful” quantum computer, one that “solves an impactful problem that we would not have been able to solve otherwise.”
He adds, “People will naturally discount my opinions, but I have spent a lot of time quantitatively comparing what we are doing with others.”
Could PyQuantum really be leading all the competition “by a wide margin”, as Taylor claims?
I don’t know.
I’m certainly not going to advise my friend or anyone else to invest in quantum computers.
But I trust Taylor, just as I trust Johnson.

passages.name: 2022 天津卷（第一次·3月） 阅读C

paras.en: The question, “What do elephants and fish have in common?” may sound strange but researchers have found that they both have a feature not observed in any other creature.
A team at Georgia Institute of Technology has discovered that elephants use a special form of air suction (吸力) in their trunks to pick up food and handle delicate objects.
Animals using suction to handle objects are typically found in water.
Many fish perform suction feeding that requires specialised body parts to quickly generate air pressure that can draw nearby food into their mouths.
The researchers have found that an elephant could do the same thanks to its huge nostrils (鼻孔) and lung capacity.
The radius (半径) of an elephant’s nostrils can increase by up to 30%, and the volume of air that it can push through its trunk increases by 64%.
This allows it to take in air at 30 times the speed of a human sneeze, enabling it to drink 3L of water a second.
In an experiment at Atlanta zoo, the researchers looked at how an elephant would pick up a small crispy (酥脆的) pancake, which was only 0.5mm thick.
The force required to break the pancake was less than 1% of the trunk’s weight (about 100kg).

The elephant was found to either use suction at a fixed distance from the pancake to “raise” the object in the air and hold it, or gently press the tip of its trunk against the pancake and apply suction to pick it up.
At no time during the experiment did the elephant break the pancake.
The researchers believe that the findings could help technology companies develop better machines that use air to do their jobs, as suction has long been used in robotics to grab objects.
The fascinating part of the study for robotics is that elephants can use air suction both on ground and in water.
The researchers are so impressed that they suggest the elephant’s suction technique could help improve robotics technology.
Nature never ceases to surprise.
Indeed, it is thought that over four-fifths of living species on earth remain undiscovered.
That is a reminder of how little we know of our planet, and that we are not the only creatures with hidden complexities.

passages.name: 2022 天津卷（第一次·3月） 阅读D

paras.en: Some scientists insist that once we discover the truth about the world, we are done.
Anyone who denies such truths, they suggest, is stupid or ignorant (无知的).
Well, no.
In science, what we do is both hard and, often, hard to explain.
The history of science offers many examples of matters that scientists thought they had resolved, only to discover that these matters needed to be reconsidered.
Familiar examples include Earth as the center of the universe and the stability of continents.
Science is a process of learning and discovery, and sometimes we learn that what we thought was right is wrong.
To say that science is “true” or “permanent” is like saying that “beauty is absolute.”
At best, it’s a bit off-key (不恰当的).
The concept of beauty today is very different from what it was in ancient Greece or the Middle Ages, and so are most of our “laws” of nature.
Other scientists may say scientific findings are true because they use “the scientific method.”
But we can never actually agree on what that method is.
Some will say it is observation and description of the world.
Others will say it is the use of experience and experiment.
Recently a leading scientist said the scientific method was to avoid fooling oneself into thinking something is true that is not.
Each of these views has its value, but if the claim is that any one of these is the scientific method, then they all fail.
History and philosophy have shown that the idea of a singular (唯一的) scientific method is unscientific.
In fact, the methods of science have varied between disciplines and across time.
Scientists have bitterly argued about which methods are the best, and, as we all know, bitter arguments rarely get resolved.
In my view, science is not simple, and neither is the natural world.
Our efforts to understand and explain the natural world are just that: efforts.
Because we’re human, we often fall flat.
The good news is that when that happens, we pick ourselves up, brush ourselves off, and get back to work.
Understanding the world we live in, and using that knowledge to do useful things, is its own reward.

passages.name: 2022 天津卷（第二次·6月） 阅读C

paras.en: Is it true that our brain alone is responsible for human cognition(认知)?
What about our body?
Is it possible for thought and behavior to originate from somewhere other than our brain?
Psychologists who study Embodied Cognition (EC) ask similar questions.
The EC theory suggests our body is also responsible for thinking or problem-solving.
More precisely, the mind shapes the body and the body shapes the mind in equal measure.
If you think about it for a moment, it makes total sense.
When you smell something good or hear amusing sounds, certain emotions are awakened.
Think about how newborns use their senses to understand the world around them.
They don’t have emotions so much as needs—they don’t feel sad, they’re just hungry and need food.
Even unborn babies can feel their mothers’ heartbeats and this has a calming effect.
In the real world, they cry when they’re cold and then get hugged.
That way, they start to associate being warm with being loved.
Understandably, theorists have been arguing for years and still disagree on whether the brain is the nerve centre that operates the rest of the body.

Older Western philosophers and mainstream language researchers believe this is fact, while EC theorises that the brain and body are working together as an organic supercomputer, processing everything and forming your reactions.
Further studies have backed up the mind-body interaction.
In one experiment, test subjects(实验对象) were asked to judge people after being handed a hot or a cold drink.
They all made warm evaluations when their fingertips perceived warmth rather than coolness.
And it works the other way too; in another study, subjects’ fingertip temperatures were measured after being“included” in or “rejected” from a group task.
Those who were included felt physically warmer.
For further proof, we can look at the metaphors(比喻说法) that we use without even thinking.
A kind and sympathetic person is frequently referred to as one with a soft heart and someone who is very strong and calm in difficult situations is often described as solid as a rock.
And this kind of metaphorical use is common across languages.
Now that you have the knowledge of mind-body interaction, why not use it?
If you’re having a bad day, a warm cup of tea will give you a flash of pleasure.
If you know you’re physically cold, warm up before making any interpersonal decisions.

passages.name: 2022 天津卷（第二次·6月） 阅读D

paras.en: Ralph Emerson once said that the purpose of life is not to be happy, but to be useful, to be loving, to make some difference in the world.
While we appreciate such words of wisdom, we rarely try to follow them in our lives.
Most people prefer to live a good life themselves, ignoring their responsibilities for the world.
This narrow perception of a good life may provide short-term benefits, but is sure to lead to long-term harm and suffering.
A good life based on comfort and luxury may eventually lead to more pain because we spoil our health and even our character, principles, ideals, and relationships.
What then, is the secret of a good life?
A good life is a process, not a state of being: a direction, not a destination.
We have to earn a good life by first serving others without any expectation in return because their happiness is the very source of our own happiness.
More importantly, we must know ourselves inside out.
Only when we examine ourselves deeply can we discover our abilities and recognize our limitations, and then work accordingly to create a better world.
The first requirement for a good life is having a loving heart.
When we do certain right things merely as a duty, we find our job so tiresome that we’ll soon burn out.
However, when we do that same job out of love, we not only enjoy what we do, but also do it with an effortless feeling.
However, love alone is insufficient to lead a good life.
Love sometimes blinds us to the reality.
Consequently, our good intentions may not lead to good results.
To achieve desired outcome, those who want to do good to others also need to equip themselves with accurate world knowledge.
False knowledge is more dangerous than ignorance.
If love is the engine of a car, knowledge is the steering wheel(方向盘).
If the engine lacks power, the car can’t move; if the driver loses control of the steering, a road accident probably occurs.
Only with love in heart and the right knowledge in mind can we lead a good life.
With love and knowledge, we go all out to create a better world by doing good to others.
When we see the impact of our good work on the world we give meaning to our life and earn lasting joy and happiness.
Conservationists go to war over whether humans are the measure of nature’s value.
New Conservationists argue such trade-offs are necessary in this human-dominated epoch.
And they support “re-wilding”, a concept originally proposed by Soule where people curtail economic growth and withdraw from landscapes, which then return to nature.
New Conservationists believe the withdrawal could happen together with economic growth.
The California-based Breakthrough Institute believes in a future where most people live in cities and rely less on natural resources for economic growth.
They would get food from industrial agriculture, including genetically modified foods, desalination, intensified meat production and aquaculture, all of which have a smaller land footprint.
And they would get their energy from renewables and natural gas.
Driving these profound shifts would be greater efficiency of production, where more products could be manufactured from fewer inputs.
And some unsustainable commodities would be replaced in the market by other, greener ones—natural gas for coal, for instance, explained Michael Shellenberger, president of the Breakthrough Institute.
Nature would, in essence, be decoupled from the economy.
And then he added a caveat: “We are not suggesting decoupling as the paradigm to save the world, or that it solves all the problems or eliminates all the trade-offs.”
Cynics (悲观者) may say all this sounds too utopian, but Breakthrough maintains the world is already on this path toward decoupling.
Nowhere is this more evident than in the United States, according to Iddo Wernick, a research scholar at the Rockefeller University, who has examined the nation’s use of 100 main commodities.
Wernick and his colleagues looked at data carefully from the U.S. Geological Survey National Minerals Information Center, which keeps a record of commodities used from 1900 through the present day.
They found that the use of 36 commodities (sand, iron ore, cotton, etc.) in the U.S. economy had peaked.
Another 53 commodities (nitrogen, timber, beef, etc.) are being used more efficiently per dollar value of gross domestic product than in the pre-1970s era.
Their use would peak soon, Wernick said.

Only 11 commodities (industrial diamond, indium, chicken, etc.) are increasing in use (Greenwire, Nov. 6), and most of these are employed by industries in small quantities to improve systems processes.
Chicken use is rising because people are eating less beef, a desirable development since poultry cultivation has a smaller environmental footprint.
The numbers show the United States has not intensified resource consumption since the 1970s even while increasing its GDP and population, said Jesse Ausubel of the Rockefeller University.
“It seems like the 20th-century expectation we had, we were always assuming the future entailed greater consumption of resources,” Ausubel said.
“But what we are seeing in the developed countries is, of course, peaks.”
Business innovation is an organization’s process for introducing new ideas, workflows, methodologies, services or products.

Like IT innovation, which calls for using technology in new ways to create a more efficient and agile organization, business innovation should enable the achievement of goals across the entire organization, with sights set on accomplishing core business aims and initiatives.

Innovation often begins with idea generation, wherein ideas are narrowed down during brainstorming sessions, after which leaders consider the business viability, feasibility and desirability of each idea.
Business innovation should improve on existing products, services or processes; or it should solve a problem; or it should reach new customers.

Recent examples of business innovation include the introduction of the Dyson vacuum cleaner, whose creator and namesake James Dyson declared in advertisements that he set out to build a better product by applying industrial cyclone technologies to the household appliance.
The purpose of the business innovation process is to create value for the organization.

That value can come from creating new revenue opportunities or driving more revenue through existing channels; from creating efficiencies that save time, money or both; or from improvements to productivity or performance.
In short, innovation should lead to higher profits.

Additionally, the results of an organization’s innovation process should yield a competitive advantage; it should help the organization to grow and reach—or, better still, exceed—strategic objectives.
Innovation and invention are closely linked, but the two terms are not interchangeable.
An invention is an entirely new creation.

The process of business innovation can produce an invention, but the term is broader in scope and includes the application of an existing concept or practice in a new way, or applying new technology to an existing product or process to improve upon it.
To better understand the difference, consider this: The telephone is an invention, but the smartphone is an innovation.
Business innovation can also be classified as either revolutionary or evolutionary.
Revolutionary business innovation yields a drastic change in a product, service, process, etc., which often destroys or supplants an existing business model.
This is also known as radical innovation.
Evolutionary or incremental innovation involves smaller, more continuous improvements that, while important, are not drastic enough to shift a company or market into a new paradigm.

Disruptive innovation is a category that emphasizes the destructive aspect of revolutionary innovation; this term applies to business innovation that leads to the creation of a new market that displaces an existing one or, similarly, a significant upheaval in a category of products or services.
Business innovation, like most business initiatives, has both benefits and risks.

Organizations should recognize on the negative side that the business innovation process can be a costly undertaking that does not always produce a return on investment (ROI); that ideas considered likely to succeed could still fail; and that stakeholders could fight the changes required to be successful.
On the other hand, organizations need to weigh those risks against the benefits of business innovation.
The benefits of regular exercise are well documented but there’s a new bonus to add to the ever-growing list.

New researchers found that middle-aged women who were physically fit could be nearly 90 percent less likely to develop dementia in later life, and as they did, it came on a decade later than less sporty women.

Lead researcher Dr. Helena Horder, of the University of Gothenburg in Sweden, said: “These findings are exciting because it’s possible that improving people’s cardiovascular (心血管的) fitness in middle age could delay or even prevent them from developing dementia. “
For the study, 191 women with an average age of 50 took a bicycle exercise test until they were exhausted to measure their peak (最大值的) cardiovascular capacity.
The average peak workload was measured at 103 watts.
A total of 40 women met the criteria for a high fitness level, or 120 watts or higher.

A total of 92 women were in the medium fitness category; and 59 women were in the low fitness category, defined as a peak workload of 80 watts or less, or having their exercise tests stopped because of high blood pressure, chest pain or other cardiovascular problems.
These women were then tested for dementia six times over the following four decades.
During that time, 44 of the women developed dementia.
Five percent of the highly fit women developed dementia, compared to 25 percent of the women with medium fitness and 32 percent of the women with low fitness.
“However, this study does not show cause and effect between cardiovascular fitness and dementia, it only shows an association.
More research is needed to see if improved fitness could have a positive effect on the risk of dementia and also to look at when during a lifetime a high fitness level is most important.”
She also admitted that a relatively small number of women were studied, all of whom were from Sweden, so the results might not be applicable to other groups.
Many people believe that working to the maximum is the secret to success, but research has found that moderation (适度) also gets results on the job.
In a study led by Ellen Langer of Harvard University, researchers asked people to translate sentences into a new made-up language.
Subjects who practiced the language moderately beforehand made fewer errors than those who practiced extensively or not at all.
High levels of knowledge can make people too attached to traditional ways of viewing problems across fields: the arts, sciences, and politics.
High conscientiousness is related to lower job performance, especially in simple jobs where it doesn’t pay to be a perfectionist.
How long we stay on the clock and how we spend that time are under careful examination in many workplaces.
The young banker who eats lunch at his desk is probably seen as a go-getter, while his colleagues who chat over a relaxed conference-room meal get dirty looks from the corner office.

“People from cultures that value relationships more than ours does are shocked by the thought of eating alone in front of a computer,” says Art Markman, a professor of psychology at the University of Texas, Austin.
Social interaction has been shown to lift mood (情绪) and get people thinking in new directions and in ways that could help improve any post-lunch effort.
Markman also promotes off-task time.
“Part of being a good thinker is experiencing things that are seemingly unrelated to what you are working on at the moment but give you fresh ideas about your work,” he says.
“Also, there is a lot of research showing that a positive mood leads to higher levels of productivity and creativity.
So, when people do things to increase their life satisfaction, they also make themselves more effective at work.”

passages.name: 2023 全国新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读C
passages.title: 《数字极简主义》一书的结构介绍
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与生活
passages.summary: 作者介绍了本书的目标和结构。第一部分阐述数字极简主义的理念基础，并介绍“数字清理”方法：先在30天里远离非必需的网络活动，再加回少量精心挑选的活动；作者还会借鉴自己2018年开展的一项有1600多人参与的实验。第二部分探讨独处的重要性、培养高质量休闲活动的必要性等问题，每章最后附有帮助读者付诸行动的实践方法。

paras.en: The goal of this book is to make the case for digital minimalism, including a detailed exploration of what it asks and why it works, and then to teach you how to adopt this philosophy if you decide it’s right for you.
paras.zh: 本书的目标是论证数字极简主义的合理性，包括详细探讨它有哪些要求、为什么有效；然后，如果你认定这一理念适合你，再教你如何践行它。

w.m: 论证……的合理性；为……提出论据

paras.en: To do so, I divided the book into two parts.
paras.zh: 为此，我把本书分成了两部分。

paras.en: In part one, I describe the philosophical foundations of digital minimalism, starting with an examination of the forces that are making so many people’s digital lives increasingly intolerable, before moving on to a detailed discussion of the digital minimalism philosophy.
paras.zh: 在第一部分，我阐述了数字极简主义的理念基础：先考察有哪些力量正让这么多人的数字生活变得越来越难以忍受，然后转入详细讨论数字极简主义理念。

paras.en: Part one concludes by introducing my suggested method for adopting this philosophy: the digital declutter.
paras.zh: 第一部分最后介绍了我推荐用来践行这一理念的方法：数字清理。

paras.en: This process requires you to step away from optional online activities for thirty days.
paras.zh: 这一过程要求你在30天里远离非必需的网络活动。

w.m: adj. 可选择的；非必需的

paras.en: At the end of the thirty days, you will then add back a small number of carefully chosen online activities that you believe will provide massive benefits to the things you value.
paras.zh: 30天结束时，你再把少量精心挑选的网络活动重新加回来——你相信这些活动会给你所看重的事物带来巨大的益处。

paras.en: In the final chapter of part one, I’ll guide you through carrying out your own digital declutter.
paras.zh: 在第一部分的最后一章，我将指导你完成自己的数字清理。

paras.en: In doing so, I’ll draw on an experiment I ran in 2018 in which over 1,600 people agreed to perform a digital declutter.
paras.zh: 在此过程中，我将借鉴自己2018年开展的一项实验：当时有1600多人同意进行数字清理。

paras.en: You’ll hear these participants’ stories and learn what strategies worked well for them, and what traps they encountered that you should avoid.
paras.zh: 你将听到这些参与者的故事，了解哪些策略对他们很有效，以及他们遇到了哪些你应当避开的陷阱。

paras.en: The second part of this book takes a closer look at some ideas that will help you cultivate (培养) a sustainable digital minimalism lifestyle.
paras.zh: 本书第二部分会更深入地探讨一些理念，它们将帮助你培养一种可持续的数字极简主义生活方式。

paras.en: In these chapters, I examine issues such as the importance of solitude (独处) and the necessity of cultivating high-quality leisure to replace the time most now spend on mindless device use.
paras.zh: 在这几章中，我探讨了一些问题，例如独处的重要性，以及培养高质量休闲活动的必要性——用这些休闲活动来取代如今大多数人花在无意识地使用电子设备上的时间。

w.m: adj. 不动脑筋的；无意识的

paras.en: Each chapter concludes with a collection of practices, which are designed to help you act on the big ideas of the chapter.
paras.zh: 每一章都以一组实践方法收尾，这些方法旨在帮助你把本章的重要理念付诸行动。

paras.en: You can view these practices as a toolbox meant to aid your efforts to build a minimalist lifestyle that works for your particular circumstances.
paras.zh: 你可以把这些实践方法看作一个工具箱，用来帮助你努力打造一种适合自身特定情况的极简主义生活方式。

passages.name: 2023 全国新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读D
passages.title: 小组讨论让“群体智慧”更准确
passages.genre: 说明文 · 心理与社会
passages.summary: 1907年，高尔顿发表论文，其估算实验表明，在某些情况下，大量独立估计的平均值可以相当准确，这被称为“群体智慧”效应：人们的误差并不总是相同，平均后相互抵消；但若误差相互关联，准确度就会下降。纳瓦哈斯主导的新研究发现，把人群分成可以讨论的小组，各组平均值比同等数量独立个人的平均值更准确；各小组最常反映的是，他们交流了论据、共同推理。这些研究虽有局限，许多问题也尚待解答，但对群体讨论和决策的潜在意义巨大。

paras.en: On March 7, 1907, the English statistician Francis Galton published a paper which illustrated what has come to be known as the “wisdom of crowds” effect.
paras.zh: 1907年3月7日，英国统计学家弗朗西斯·高尔顿发表了一篇论文，阐释了后来被称为“群体智慧”效应的现象。

paras.en: The estimation experiment he conducted showed that in some cases, the average of a large number of independent estimates could be quite accurate.
paras.zh: 他所做的估算实验表明，在某些情况下，大量独立估计的平均值可以相当准确。

paras.en: This effect capitalizes on the fact that when people make errors, those errors aren’t always the same.
paras.zh: 这一效应利用了这样一个事实：人们出错时，误差并不总是相同的。

paras.en: Some people will tend to overestimate, and some to underestimate.
paras.zh: 有些人往往会高估，有些人则往往会低估。

paras.en: When enough of these errors are averaged together, they cancel each other out, resulting in a more accurate estimate.
paras.zh: 把足够多的这类误差平均起来时，它们就会相互抵消，从而得出更准确的估计。

paras.en: If people are similar and tend to make the same errors, then their errors won’t cancel each other out.
paras.zh: 如果人们彼此相似、往往犯同样的错误，那么他们的误差就不会相互抵消。

paras.en: In more technical terms, the wisdom of crowds requires that people’s estimates be independent.
paras.zh: 用更专业的话来说，群体智慧要求人们的估计是相互独立的。

w.m: v. 要求（that从句用虚拟语气）

paras.en: If, for whatever reasons, people’s errors become correlated or dependent, the accuracy of the estimate will go down.
paras.zh: 无论出于什么原因，只要人们的误差变得相互关联或相互依赖，估计的准确度就会下降。

w.m: adj. 相关的；相互关联的
adj. 依赖的；相互依赖的

paras.en: But a new study led by Joaquin Navajas offered an interesting twist (转折) on this classic phenomenon.
paras.zh: 但华金·纳瓦哈斯主导的一项新研究为这一经典现象带来了一个有趣的新转折。

paras.en: The key finding of the study was that when crowds were further divided into smaller groups that were allowed to have a discussion, the averages from these groups were more accurate than those from an equal number of independent individuals.
paras.zh: 这项研究的关键发现是：如果把人群进一步分成可以进行讨论的小组，这些小组得出的平均值就比同等数量的独立个人得出的平均值更准确。

paras.en: For instance, the average obtained from the estimates of four discussion groups of five was significantly more accurate than the average obtained from 20 independent individuals.
paras.zh: 例如，由4个5人讨论小组的估计得出的平均值，明显比由20个独立个人得出的平均值更准确。

paras.en: In a follow-up study with 100 university students, the researchers tried to get a better sense of what the group members actually did in their discussion.
paras.zh: 在一项有100名大学生参与的后续研究中，研究人员试图更清楚地了解小组成员在讨论中实际做了什么。

paras.en: Did they tend to go with those most confident about their estimates?
paras.zh: 他们是否往往会听从那些对自己的估计最有把握的人？

paras.en: Did they follow those least willing to change their minds?
paras.zh: 他们是否会听从那些最不愿意改变主意的人？

paras.en: This happened some of the time, but it wasn’t the dominant response.
paras.zh: 这种情况有时确实发生，但并不是主要的反应。

w.m: adj. 主要的；占主导地位的

paras.en: Most frequently, the groups reported that they “shared arguments and reasoned together”.
paras.zh: 各小组最常反映的是，他们“交流了论据，并一起进行推理”。

paras.en: Somehow, these arguments and this reasoning resulted in a global reduction in error.
paras.zh: 不知何故，这些论据和推理使误差在整体上减少了。

w.m: adv. 不知怎么地；以某种方式

paras.en: Although the studies led by Navajas have limitations and many questions remain, the potential implications for group discussion and decision-making are enormous.
paras.zh: 尽管纳瓦哈斯主导的这些研究存在局限，许多问题也仍未解决，但它们对群体讨论和决策的潜在影响是巨大的。

w.m: v. 仍然存在；尚待解决

passages.name: 2023 全国新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读C
passages.title: 艺术作品中的书与阅读
passages.genre: 说明文 · 艺术与文化
passages.summary: 《阅读艺术：献给爱书人的艺术》收录了来自世界各地博物馆的近300件艺术作品，通过描绘书籍和阅读的场景，呈现出超越文化与时代的共同人性。书在画中可以作为象征，在印刷机普及之前本身就可能是艺术品，近来又被艺术家用作创作的原材料。文章还指出，印刷书籍虽然古老，却依然和电子阅读器一样具有互动性，并且仍能让人进行完全私密的“离线”活动。

paras.en: Reading Art: Art for Book Lovers is a celebration of an everyday object — the book, represented here in almost three hundred artworks from museums around the world.
paras.zh: 《阅读艺术：献给爱书人的艺术》是对一种日常物品——书——的礼赞；这本画册收录了来自世界各地博物馆的近300件艺术作品，书的形象就呈现在这些作品之中。

paras.en: The image of the reader appears throughout history, in art made long before books as we now know them came into being.
paras.zh: 读者的形象贯穿古今：早在我们今天所熟知的这种书籍问世很久以前，艺术作品中就已出现了读者的身影。

paras.en: In artists’ representations of books and reading, we see moments of shared humanity that go beyond culture and time.
paras.zh: 在艺术家对书籍和阅读的描绘中，我们看到了体现人类共同天性、超越文化与时代的瞬间。

paras.en: In this “book of books,” artworks are selected and arranged in a way that emphasizes these connections between different eras and cultures.
paras.zh: 在这本“书中之书”里，艺术作品的挑选和编排方式突出了不同时代、不同文化之间的这些联系。

paras.en: We see scenes of children learning to read at home or at school, with the book as a focus for relations between the generations.
paras.zh: 我们看到孩子们在家中或学校里学习阅读的场景，书在其中成为代际关系的焦点。

paras.en: Adults are portrayed (描绘) alone in many settings and poses — absorbed in a volume, deep in thought or lost in a moment of leisure.
paras.zh: 艺术家笔下的成年人则独自一人，身处各种环境，姿态各异——或沉浸在书中，或陷入沉思，或沉醉于片刻的闲暇。

paras.en: These scenes may have been painted hundreds of years ago, but they record moments we can all relate to.
paras.zh: 这些场景可能是几百年前画的，但它们记录下的是我们都能感同身受的时刻。

paras.en: Books themselves may be used symbolically in paintings to demonstrate the intellect (才智), wealth or faith of the subject.
paras.zh: 在绘画中，书本身也可能被用作象征，来展示画中人物的才智、财富或信仰。

paras.en: Before the wide use of the printing press, books were treasured objects and could be works of art in their own right.
paras.zh: 在印刷机广泛使用之前，书是人们珍视的物品，其本身就可能是艺术品。

paras.en: More recently, as books have become inexpensive or even throwaway, artists have used them as the raw material for artworks — transforming covers, pages or even complete volumes into paintings and sculptures.
paras.zh: 近来，随着书变得便宜，甚至成了用完就扔的东西，艺术家们便把书用作艺术创作的原材料——把封面、书页甚至整本书改造成绘画和雕塑。

w.m: adj. 用后即弃的；一次性的

paras.en: Continued developments in communication technologies were once believed to make the printed page outdated.
paras.zh: 人们曾经认为，通信技术的不断发展会让印刷读物过时。

paras.en: From a 21st-century point of view, the printed book is certainly ancient, but it remains as interactive as any battery-powered e-reader.
paras.zh: 从21世纪的视角来看，印刷书籍无疑是古老的，但它依然和任何一台电池驱动的电子阅读器一样具有互动性。

w.m: v. （系动词）仍然是；依然保持

paras.en: To serve its function, a book must be activated by a user: the cover opened, the pages parted, the contents reviewed, perhaps notes written down or words underlined.
paras.zh: 书要发挥作用，就必须由使用者来激活：掀开封面，翻开书页，浏览内容，或许还要记下笔记或在字词下画线。

paras.en: And in contrast to our increasingly networked lives where the information we consume is monitored and tracked, a printed book still offers the chance of a wholly private, “off-line” activity.
paras.zh: 我们的生活日益网络化，所获取的信息受到监控和追踪；与之相比，印刷书籍仍让人有机会进行完全私密的“离线”活动。

passages.name: 2023 全国新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读D
passages.title: 城市野性自然与“自然语言”
passages.genre: 说明文 · 人与自然
passages.summary: 城市迅速扩张，城市居民越来越难接触到自然。一项新研究调查了一座大型城市公园的游客，把他们与自然的有意义互动编码分类，归纳出一种“自然语言”，其中最常被提到的有六类，如邂逅野生动物、沿水边散步等。研究者希望借助这种语言把人与自然的互动带回日常生活，并指出还需要保护自然。

paras.en: As cities balloon with growth, access to nature for people living in urban areas is becoming harder to find.
paras.zh: 随着城市迅速扩张，生活在城市地区的人们正越来越难以接触到自然。

w.m: n. 接触（的机会）；使用权

paras.en: If you’re lucky, there might be a pocket park near where you live, but it’s unusual to find places in a city that are relatively wild.
paras.zh: 运气好的话，你住的地方附近可能会有一个口袋公园，但在城市里很少能找到相对原生态的地方。

w.m: n. 口袋公园（小型城市公园）
adj. 未经开发的；保持自然原貌的

paras.en: Past research has found health and wellness benefits of nature for humans, but a new study shows that wildness in urban areas is extremely important for human well-being.
paras.zh: 过去的研究已经发现自然对人类健康和身心安康有益，但一项新研究表明，城市地区的野性自然对人类福祉极其重要。

paras.en: The research team focused on a large urban park.
paras.zh: 研究团队以一座大型城市公园为研究对象。

paras.en: They surveyed several hundred park-goers, asking them to submit a written summary online of a meaningful interaction they had with nature in the park.
paras.zh: 他们调查了几百名公园游客，请他们在网上提交一份书面总结，讲述自己在公园里与自然的一次有意义的互动。

paras.en: The researchers then examined these submissions, coding (编码) experiences into different categories.
paras.zh: 研究人员随后仔细查看了这些提交的内容，把各种体验编码，归入不同的类别。

paras.en: For example, one participant’s experience of “We sat and listened to the waves at the beach for a while” was assigned the categories “sitting at beach” and “listening to waves.”
paras.zh: 例如，一位参与者的体验“我们坐在海滩上听了一会儿海浪声”，被归入“坐在海滩上”和“倾听海浪”这两个类别。

paras.en: Across the 320 submissions, a pattern of categories the researchers call a “nature language” began to emerge.
paras.zh: 在全部320份提交内容中，一种类别模式开始显现，研究人员称之为“自然语言”。

paras.en: After the coding of all submissions, half a dozen categories were noted most often as important to visitors.
paras.zh: 在对所有提交内容完成编码后，有六个类别最常被记录为对游客很重要。

paras.en: These include encountering wildlife, walking along the edge of water, and following an established trail.
paras.zh: 其中包括邂逅野生动物、沿水边散步和沿着既有的步道行走。

paras.en: Naming each nature experience creates a usable language, which helps people recognize and take part in the activities that are most satisfying and meaningful to them.
paras.zh: 为每一种自然体验命名，就形成了一种可用的语言，它能帮助人们识别并参与那些最让自己满足、对自己最有意义的活动。

paras.en: For example, the experience of walking along the edge of water might be satisfying for a young professional on a weekend hike in the park.
paras.zh: 例如，对一个周末在公园徒步的年轻上班族来说，沿水边散步的体验可能会令人满足。

w.m: n. 专业人士；职场人士

paras.en: Back downtown during a workday, they can enjoy a more domestic form of this interaction by walking along a fountain on their lunch break.
paras.zh: 等到工作日回到市中心，这位上班族可以在午休时沿着喷泉散步，以一种更人工化、不那么野性的形式享受这种互动。

w.m: adj. 驯化的；非野生的（文中指人工环境里的）

paras.en: “We’re trying to generate a language that helps bring the human-nature interactions back into our daily lives.
paras.zh: “我们正努力创造一种语言，帮助把人与自然的互动带回我们的日常生活。

paras.en: And for that to happen, we also need to protect nature so that we can interact with it,” said Peter Kahn, a senior author of the study.
paras.zh: 而要实现这一点，我们还需要保护自然，这样我们才能与之互动。”该研究的资深作者之一彼得·卡恩说。

passages.name: 2023 全国甲卷 阅读C
passages.title: 一本让我重拾哲学之爱的书
passages.genre: 议论文 · 书评
passages.summary: 作者13岁左右读《苏菲的世界》爱上了哲学，但上大学后，那些自以为比别人更懂哲学家、还要给人讲解的人让这份热爱消失了。埃里克·韦纳的《苏格拉底快车》重新唤起了作者对哲学的热爱：这本书不是讲解哲学，而是邀请读者思考和体验哲学，学会运用哲学来改善生活。作者认为此书有趣而犀利，值得花时间一读。

paras.en: I was about 13 when an uncle gave me a copy of Jostein Gaarder’s Sophie’s World.
paras.zh: 我13岁左右的时候，一位叔叔送给我一本乔斯坦·贾德的《苏菲的世界》。

paras.en: It was full of ideas that were new to me, so I spent the summer with my head in and out of that book.
paras.zh: 书中满是我从未接触过的思想，所以整个夏天我都时而埋头读这本书，时而又从书中抬起头来。

w.m: 时而进入时而离开；进进出出

paras.en: It spoke to me and brought me into a world of philosophy (哲学).
paras.zh: 它打动了我，把我带进了哲学的世界。

paras.en: That love for philosophy lasted until I got to college.
paras.zh: 这份对哲学的热爱一直持续到我上大学。

paras.en: Nothing kills the love for philosophy faster than people who think they understand Foucault, Baudrillard, or Confucius better than you — and then try to explain them.
paras.zh: 最能迅速扼杀对哲学的热爱的，莫过于那些自以为比你更懂福柯、鲍德里亚或孔子的人——接着还要试图给你讲解这些哲学家的思想。

w.m: 没有什么比……更快（最……莫过于）

paras.en: Eric Weiner’s The Socrates Express: In Search of Life Lessons from Dead Philosophers reawakened my love for philosophy.
paras.zh: 埃里克·韦纳的《苏格拉底快车：向已故哲学家寻求人生启示》重新唤起了我对哲学的热爱。

paras.en: It is not an explanation but an invitation to think about and experience philosophy.
paras.zh: 这本书不是讲解，而是邀请——邀请人们去思考、去体验哲学。

paras.en: Weiner starts each chapter with a scene on a train ride between cities and then frames each philosopher’s work in the context (背景) of one thing they can help us do better.
paras.zh: 韦纳在每一章的开头都描写一段城际火车旅途中的场景，然后围绕每位哲学家能帮助我们做得更好的某一件事，来阐述这位哲学家的思想著述。

w.m: n. 乘坐（交通工具）；旅程

paras.en: The end result is a read in which we learn to wonder like Socrates, see like Thoreau, listen like Schopenhauer, and have no regrets like Nietzsche.
paras.zh: 最终的成果是这样一本读物：我们从中学会像苏格拉底那样好奇，像梭罗那样观察，像叔本华那样倾听，像尼采那样不留遗憾。

paras.en: This, more than a book about understanding philosophy, is a book about learning to use philosophy to improve a life.
paras.zh: 与其说这是一本关于理解哲学的书，不如说它是一本关于学会运用哲学来改善生活的书。

paras.en: He makes philosophical thought an appealing exercise that improves the quality of our experiences, and he does so with plenty of humor.
paras.zh: 他把哲学思考变成一项引人入胜的思维活动，能提升我们种种体验的品质，而且他的笔调充满幽默。

paras.en: Weiner enters into conversation with some of the most important philosophers in history, and he becomes part of that crowd in the process by decoding (解读) their messages and adding his own interpretation.
paras.zh: 韦纳与历史上一些最重要的哲学家展开对话，并在此过程中解读他们传达的思想、加入自己的阐释，从而成为他们当中的一员。

paras.en: The Socrates Express is a fun, sharp book that draws readers in with its apparent simplicity and gradually pulls them into deeper thoughts on desire, loneliness, and aging.
paras.zh: 《苏格拉底快车》是一本有趣而犀利的书，它以看似简单的面貌吸引读者，再逐渐把他们带入对欲望、孤独和衰老更深入的思考。

paras.en: The invitation is clear: Weiner wants you to pick up a coffee or tea and sit down with this book.
paras.zh: 这份邀请很明确：韦纳希望你端起一杯咖啡或茶，坐下来读这本书。

paras.en: I encourage you to take his offer.
paras.zh: 我鼓励你接受他的邀请。

paras.en: It’s worth your time, even if time is something we don’t have a lot of.
paras.zh: 这本书值得你花时间去读，即使我们的时间并不充裕。

passages.name: 2023 全国甲卷 阅读D
passages.title: 灰熊回归与人熊共处
passages.genre: 说明文 · 人与自然
passages.summary: 灰熊既令美国人敬畏又让人害怕。经过几个世纪的猎杀，灰熊一度只剩600到800只，1975年被列入《濒危物种法》保护名录；如今美国本土48个州约有2000只，正重新占据以前的活动范围，人们也越来越多地见到它们。美国鱼类及野生动植物管理局曾两次试图将其从保护名录中除名，但两次都因自然保护组织提起的诉讼而被推翻。文章指出，只要人们清走院子和营地里的食物及引诱物，灰熊通常只是路过，不会惹麻烦；在鸡舍等家畜圈舍周围安装电围栏也能有效让灰熊远离。

paras.en: Grizzly bears, which may grow to about 2.5 m long and weigh over 400 kg, occupy a conflicted corner of the American psyche — we revere (敬畏) them even as they give us frightening dreams.
paras.zh: 灰熊体长可达约2.5米，体重可超过400千克，它们在美国人的内心深处占据着一个充满矛盾的角落——我们一面敬畏它们，一面又被它们吓得做噩梦。

w.m: adj. 令人恐惧的；可怕的

paras.en: Ask the tourists from around the world that flood into Yellowstone National Park what they most hope to see, and their answer is often the same: a grizzly bear.
paras.zh: 问问那些从世界各地涌入黄石国家公园的游客最希望看到什么，他们的回答往往是一样的：灰熊。

paras.en: “Grizzly bears are re-occupying large areas of their former range,” says bear biologist Chris Servheen.
paras.zh: “灰熊正在重新占据它们以前活动范围内的大片区域，”熊类生物学家克里斯·瑟文说。

w.m: n. （动物的）活动范围；分布区

paras.en: As grizzly bears expand their range into places where they haven’t been seen in a century or more, they’re increasingly being sighted by humans.
paras.zh: 随着灰熊把活动范围扩展到一个世纪甚至更久都不见其踪影的地方，人们越来越多地目击到它们。

paras.en: The western half of the U.S. was full of grizzlies when Europeans came, with a rough number of 50,000 or more living alongside Native Americans.
paras.zh: 欧洲人到来时，美国西半部到处都是灰熊，粗略估计有5万只甚至更多，与美洲原住民比邻而居。

paras.en: By the early 1970s, after centuries of cruel and continuous hunting by settlers, 600 to 800 grizzlies remained on a mere 2 percent of their former range in the Northern Rockies.
paras.zh: 到20世纪70年代初，在遭受定居者几个世纪残酷而持续的猎杀之后，仅剩600到800只灰熊，分布在北落基山脉一带，所占区域只有它们以前活动范围的2%。

paras.en: In 1975, grizzlies were listed under the Endangered Species Act.
paras.zh: 1975年，灰熊被列入《濒危物种法》的保护名录。

w.m: n. 法令；（立法机关通过的）法律

paras.en: Today, there are about 2,000 grizzly bears in the lower 48 states.
paras.zh: 如今，美国本土48个州约有2000只灰熊。

paras.en: Their recovery has been so successful that the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service has twice attempted to delist grizzlies, which would loosen legal protections and allow them to be hunted.
paras.zh: 灰熊恢复得如此成功，以至于美国鱼类及野生动植物管理局已两次试图将其从保护名录中除名，此举会放松对灰熊的法律保护，并允许人们猎杀它们。

paras.en: Both efforts were overturned due to lawsuits from conservation groups.
paras.zh: 这两次尝试都因自然保护组织提起的诉讼而被推翻。

paras.en: For now, grizzlies remain listed.
paras.zh: 目前，灰熊仍在保护名录之中。

paras.en: Obviously, if precautions (预防) aren’t taken, grizzlies can become troublesome, sometimes killing farm animals or walking through yards in search of food.
paras.zh: 显然，如果不采取预防措施，灰熊可能会变得令人头疼，有时会咬死家畜，或者为了寻找食物而穿过人们的院子。

w.m: adj. 令人头疼的；麻烦的

paras.en: If people remove food and attractants from their yards and campsites, grizzlies will typically pass by without trouble.
paras.zh: 如果人们把食物和引诱物从院子和营地里清走，灰熊通常只是经过，不会惹麻烦。

paras.en: Putting electric fencing around chicken houses and other farm animal quarters is also highly effective at keeping grizzlies away.
paras.zh: 在鸡舍和其他家畜圈舍周围安装电围栏，也能非常有效地让灰熊远离。

paras.en: “Our hope is to have a clean, attractant-free place where bears can pass through without learning bad habits,” says James Jonkel, a longtime biologist who manages bears in and around Missoula.
paras.zh: “我们希望有一个干净、没有引诱物的地方，让熊可以穿行而过，而不会养成坏习惯，”詹姆斯·琼克尔说，他是一位从业多年的生物学家，负责管理米苏拉及其周边地区的熊。

passages.name: 2023 全国乙卷 阅读C
passages.title: 电视厨师改变英国人的烹饪习惯
passages.genre: 说明文 · 饮食与社会
passages.summary: 英国菜肴向来名声不佳，但英国正涌现出越来越多的顶级电视厨师。据报道，坚持传统饮食的人在减少，一项新研究显示，五分之一的英国人表示烹饪节目促使他们尝试不同的食物，近三分之一的人现在使用的配料种类比过去更多，四分之一的成年人说电视厨师让他们对拓展烹饪知识和技能更有信心。电视上烹饪类节目播出得更频繁，男厨师也越来越多，男孩喜欢做饭不再被视为“不酷”。

paras.en: What comes into your mind when you think of British food?
paras.zh: 一想到英国菜，你脑海里会浮现出什么？

paras.en: Probably fish and chips, or a Sunday dinner of meat and two vegetables.
paras.zh: 大概是炸鱼薯条，或者周日一份肉配两样蔬菜的正餐吧。

paras.en: But is British food really so uninteresting?
paras.zh: 但英国菜真的这么乏味吗？

paras.en: Even though Britain has a reputation for less-than-impressive cuisine, it is producing more top-class chefs who appear frequently on our television screens and whose recipe books frequently top the bestseller lists.
paras.zh: 尽管英国菜肴的名声向来不怎么样，但英国正涌现出越来越多的顶级厨师，他们频频出现在我们的电视屏幕上，写的菜谱书也常常高居畅销书榜首。

w.m: adj. 不怎么出色的；平庸的

paras.en: It’s thanks to these TV chefs rather than any advertising campaign that Britons are turning away from meat-and-two-veg and ready-made meals and becoming more adventurous in their cooking habits.
paras.zh: 英国人正逐渐告别“一肉两菜”和现成餐食，在烹饪习惯上也变得更敢于尝试，这要归功于这些电视厨师，而不是什么广告宣传。

w.m: adj. 敢于尝试的；爱冒险的

paras.en: It has recently been reported that the number of those sticking to a traditional diet is slowly declining and around half of Britain’s consumers would like to change or improve their cooking in some way.
paras.zh: 据最近报道，坚持传统饮食的人数正在缓慢下降，约一半的英国消费者想在某些方面改变或改进自己的烹饪方式。

paras.en: There has been a rise in the number of students applying for food courses at UK universities and colleges.
paras.zh: 申请英国各大学和学院食品类课程的学生人数有所增加。

paras.en: It seems that TV programmes have helped change what people think about cooking.
paras.zh: 看来，电视节目促使人们改变了对烹饪的看法。

paras.en: According to a new study from market analysts, 1 in 5 Britons say that watching cookery programmes on TV has encouraged them to try different food.
paras.zh: 据市场分析人士的一项新研究，五分之一的英国人表示，看电视上的烹饪节目促使他们尝试了不同的食物。

paras.en: Almost one third say they now use a wider variety of ingredients (配料) than they used to, and just under 1 in 4 say they now buy better quality ingredients than before.
paras.zh: 近三分之一的人说，他们现在使用的配料种类比过去更多；略低于四分之一的人说，他们现在买的配料质量比以前更好。

paras.en: One in four adults say that TV chefs have made them much more confident about expanding their cookery knowledge and skills, and young people are also getting more interested in cooking.
paras.zh: 四分之一的成年人说，电视厨师让他们在拓展烹饪知识和技能方面自信了许多；年轻人也对烹饪越来越感兴趣。

paras.en: The UK’s obsession (痴迷) with food is reflected in television scheduling.
paras.zh: 英国人对美食的痴迷在电视节目编排中可见一斑。

paras.en: Cookery shows and documentaries about food are broadcast more often than before.
paras.zh: 烹饪节目和美食纪录片播出得比以前更频繁了。

paras.en: With an increasing number of male chefs on TV, it’s no longer “uncool” for boys to like cooking.
paras.zh: 随着电视上的男厨师越来越多，男孩喜欢做饭不再是“不酷”的事了。

passages.name: 2023 全国乙卷 阅读D
passages.title: 讲述世界历史不能只靠文字
passages.genre: 议论文 · 历史与文化
passages.summary: 作者认为，要讲述一部不偏重人类某一部分的世界史，不能只靠文字记载，因为世界上大部分地区在大部分时间里都没有文字。以库克船长的船队与澳大利亚原住民在植物学湾的首次冲突为例，英国人一方留下了科学报告和船长的记录，澳大利亚人一方却只留下一面木盾。作者指出，失败的一方往往只有实物能讲述他们的故事，因此要找到对话的另一半，不仅要解读文字记载，还要解读实物。

paras.en: If you want to tell the history of the whole world, a history that does not privilege one part of humanity, you cannot do it through texts alone, because only some of the world has ever had texts, while most of the world, for most of the time, has not.
paras.zh: 如果你想讲述整个世界的历史，一部不偏重人类中某一部分的历史，就不能只靠文字记载，因为世界上只有部分地区曾经有过文字，而大部分地区在大部分时间里都没有。

w.m: v. 偏重；给予……特殊待遇

paras.en: Writing is one of humanity’s later achievements, and until fairly recently even many literate (有文字的) societies recorded their concerns not only in writing but in things.
paras.zh: 文字是人类较晚取得的成就之一，而且直到相当晚近的时候，甚至许多有文字的社会也不仅用文字，还用实物来记录他们关心的事情。

paras.en: Ideally a history would bring together texts and objects, and some chapters of this book are able to do just that, but in many cases we simply can’t.
paras.zh: 理想的情况是，一部历史应当把文字记载和实物结合起来，本书有些章节恰好能做到这一点，但在许多情况下，我们根本做不到。

w.m: adv. 理想的情况是；理想地

paras.en: The clearest example of this imbalance between literate and non-literate history is perhaps the first conflict, at Botany Bay, between Captain Cook’s voyage and the Australian Aboriginals.
paras.zh: 有文字的历史与无文字的历史之间这种不平衡，最明显的例子或许是库克船长的远航船队与澳大利亚原住民在植物学湾发生的首次冲突。

w.m: n. 远航；航行（此处指远航船队）

paras.en: From the English side, we have scientific reports and the captain’s record of that terrible day.
paras.zh: 在英国人一方，我们有科学报告，还有船长对那可怕的一天的记录。

paras.en: From the Australian side, we have only a wooden shield (盾) dropped by a man in flight after his first experience of gunshot.
paras.zh: 而在澳大利亚人一方，我们只有一面木盾，那是一名男子第一次遭遇枪火后，在逃跑时丢下的。

paras.en: If we want to reconstruct what was actually going on that day, the shield must be questioned and interpreted as deeply and strictly as the written reports.
paras.zh: 如果我们想还原那天究竟发生了什么，就必须像对待书面报告那样，深入而严谨地审视和解读这面盾牌。

paras.en: In addition to the problem of miscomprehension from both sides, there are victories accidentally or deliberately twisted, especially when only the victors know how to write.
paras.zh: 除了双方相互误解的问题之外，还有一些胜利被有意无意地歪曲了，尤其是在只有胜利者会书写的情况下。

paras.en: Those who are on the losing side often have only their things to tell their stories.
paras.zh: 处于失败一方的人，往往只有自己的物品能讲述他们的故事。

paras.en: The Caribbean Taino, the Australian Aboriginals, the African people of Benin and the Incas, all of whom appear in this book, can speak to us now of their past achievements most powerfully through the objects they made: a history told through things gives them back a voice.
paras.zh: 加勒比地区的泰诺人、澳大利亚原住民、非洲的贝宁人和印加人都出现在本书中，如今，他们能够通过自己制作的实物，最有力地向我们讲述他们过去的成就：通过实物讲述的历史让他们重新发出声音。

w.m: 他们全都（非限制性定语从句）

paras.en: When we consider contact (联系) between literate and non-literate societies such as these, all our first-hand accounts are necessarily twisted, only one half of a dialogue.
paras.zh: 在考察像这样的有文字社会与无文字社会之间的接触时，我们所有的第一手记述都必然是扭曲的，只是一场对话的一半。

paras.en: If we are to find the other half of that conversation, we have to read not just the texts, but the objects.
paras.zh: 如果要找到那场对话的另一半，我们就不仅要解读文字记载，还要解读实物。

passages.name: 2023 北京卷 阅读C
passages.title: 只顾眼前：短视主义的心理根源
passages.genre: 议论文 · 社会与心理
passages.summary: 不同领域的研究者一致认为，短视主义如今是工业化社会的一个重大问题，无法关注更长远的原因和后果导致了气候变化、生物多样性崩溃等严重问题。人们存在偏向当下的倾向：在商业中表现为短视的决策，在气候变化等问题上表现为不愿在今天做出小小的牺牲。这种偏向并非由单一原因造成，但心理偏向起着重要作用，如不愿延迟满足、受当下最易获取的信息影响、过分看重喧闹紧迫的事情。在环境变化方面，人们还可能形成集体性的“记性差”，把自己所遇到的状况视为寻常。

paras.en: In recent years, researchers from diverse fields have agreed that short-termism is now a significant problem in industrialised societies.
paras.zh: 近年来，不同领域的研究者一致认为，短视主义如今已成为工业化社会的一个重大问题。

w.m: n. 短视主义；只顾眼前

paras.en: The inability to engage with longer-term causes and consequences leads to some of the world’s most serious problems: climate change, biodiversity collapse, and more.
paras.zh: 无法关注更长远的原因和后果，导致了世界上一些最严重的问题：气候变化、生物多样性崩溃，等等。

paras.en: The historian Francis Cole argues that the West has entered a period where “only the present exists, a present characterised at once by the cruelty of the instant and by the boredom of an unending now”.
paras.zh: 历史学家弗朗西斯·科尔认为，西方已进入这样一个时期：“只有当下存在，而这个当下的特征既是瞬间的残酷，又是无尽此刻的乏味”。

w.m: adj. 无尽的；没完没了的

paras.en: It has been proved that people have a bias (偏向) towards the present, focusing on loud attractions in the moment at the expense of the health, well-being and financial stability of their future selves or community.
paras.zh: 已经证实，人们存在偏向当下的倾向：他们专注于眼前喧闹的诱惑，却以牺牲未来的自己或未来社群的健康、福祉和财务稳定为代价。

w.m: n. 有吸引力的事物；诱惑

paras.en: In business, this bias surfaces as short-sighted decisions.
paras.zh: 在商业中，这种偏向表现为短视的决策。

w.m: adj. 短视的；目光短浅的

paras.en: And on slow-burning problems like climate change, it translates into the unwillingness to make small sacrifices (牺牲) today that could make a major difference tomorrow.
paras.zh: 而在气候变化这类缓慢恶化的问题上，它就表现为人们不愿在今天做出小小的牺牲，而这些牺牲可能在明天带来重大改变。

w.m: adj. 缓慢发展的；慢慢恶化的
带来（重大）改变；产生（重大）影响

paras.en: Instead, all that matters is next quarter’s profit, or satisfying some other near-term desires.
paras.zh: 相反，人们只在乎下一季度的利润，或是满足其他某些眼前的欲望。

paras.en: These biased perspectives cannot be blamed on one single cause.
paras.zh: 这些带有偏向的看法不能归咎于单一原因。

w.m: adj. 有偏向的；有偏见的

paras.en: It is fair to say, though, that our psychological biases play a major role.
paras.zh: 不过，平心而论，我们的心理偏向起着重要作用。

paras.en: People’s hesitancy to delay satisfaction is the most obvious example, but there are others.
paras.zh: 人们不愿延迟满足是最明显的例子，但例子不止这一个。

paras.en: One of them is about how the most accessible information in the present affects decisions about the future.
paras.zh: 其中一种偏向涉及当下最容易获取的信息如何影响有关未来的决策。

w.m: adj. 易获得的；可获取的

paras.en: For instance, you might hear someone say: “It’s cold this winter, so I needn’t worry about global warming.”
paras.zh: 比如，你可能会听到有人说：“今年冬天很冷，所以我不必担心全球变暖。”

paras.en: Another is that loud and urgent matters are given too much importance, making people ignore longer-term trends that arguably matter more.
paras.zh: 另一种是人们过分看重喧闹而紧迫的事情，从而忽视了那些可以说更为重要的长期趋势。

paras.en: This is when a pop star draws far more attention than, say, gradual biodiversity decline.
paras.zh: 这时就会出现这样的情况：一位流行歌星远比诸如生物多样性逐渐减少之类的问题更受关注。

paras.en: As a psychologist once joked, if aliens (外星人) wanted to weaken humanity, they wouldn’t send ships; they would invent climate change.
paras.zh: 一位心理学家曾开玩笑说，如果外星人想削弱人类，他们不会派飞船来，而是会发明气候变化。

paras.en: Indeed, when it comes to environmental transformations, we can develop a form of collective “poor memory”, and each new generation can believe the state of affairs they encounter is nothing out of the ordinary.
paras.zh: 的确，说到环境变化，我们可能会形成某种集体性的“记性差”，而每一代新人都可能认为，自己所遇到的状况没有什么不寻常。

paras.en: Older people today, for example, can remember a time with insect-covered car windscreens after long drives.
paras.zh: 比如，如今上了年纪的人能记得那样一个年代：长途驾车之后，汽车挡风玻璃上会布满昆虫。

paras.en: Children, on the other hand, have no idea that the insect population has dropped dramatically.
paras.zh: 而孩子们则不知道，昆虫的数量已经急剧下降。

passages.name: 2023 北京卷 阅读D
passages.title: 人工生命研究的意义与困境
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科学与探索
passages.summary: 人工生命（ALife）领域试图系统地阐明生命的基本原理，但迄今还没有人令人信服地造出人工生命，因而这一领域容易招致批评；研究者艾伦·史密斯认为，追问其“意义”可能根本就没抓住要点。作者指出，这一研究可能带来实际回报，例如有望催生真正具有创造性的机器；但由于核心概念“生命”尚无定义、研究者之间又缺乏共识，其进展比人工智能更难辨识。作者认为，ALife的发展恰恰映照出生命演化本身，它的兴起或许也终将被证明是不可避免的。

paras.en: What is life?
paras.zh: 生命是什么？

paras.en: Like most great questions, this one is easy to ask but difficult to answer.
paras.zh: 和大多数重大问题一样，这个问题问起来容易，回答起来却很难。

paras.en: The reason is simple: we know of just one type of life and it’s challenging to do science with a sample size of one.
paras.zh: 原因很简单：我们只知道一种生命，而在样本量只有一个的情况下做科学研究很有挑战性。

paras.en: The field of artificial life — called ALife for short — is the systematic attempt to spell out life’s fundamental principles.
paras.zh: 人工生命（简称ALife）这一领域，是一种系统性的尝试，旨在阐明生命的基本原理。

paras.en: Many of its practitioners, so-called ALifers, think that somehow making life is the surest way to really understand what life is.
paras.zh: 该领域的许多从业者，也就是所谓的ALifer（人工生命研究者），认为设法造出生命是真正理解生命为何物的最可靠途径。

paras.en: So far no one has convincingly made artificial life.
paras.zh: 迄今为止，还没有人令人信服地造出人工生命。

paras.en: This track record makes ALife a ripe target for criticism, such as declarations of the field’s doubtful scientific value.
paras.zh: 这样的过往记录使ALife成了现成的批评靶子，比如有人宣称这一领域的科学价值值得怀疑。

w.m: adj. 正适合（成为……）的；（时机）成熟的
adj. 令人怀疑的；不确定的

paras.en: Alan Smith, a complexity scientist, is tired of such complaints.
paras.zh: 复杂性科学家艾伦·史密斯已经厌倦了这类抱怨。

paras.en: Asking about “the point” of ALife might be, well, missing the point entirely, he says.
paras.zh: 他说，追问ALife有什么“意义”，或许，嗯，完全没抓住要点。

paras.en: “The existence of a living system is not about the use of anything,” Alan says.
paras.zh: “生命系统的存在与它有没有用无关，”艾伦说。
