paras.en: “Some people ask me, ‘So what’s the worth of artificial life?’
paras.zh: “有人问我：‘那么，人工生命有什么价值呢？’

paras.en: Do you ever think, ‘What is the worth of your grandmother?’”
paras.zh: 你会不会去想：‘你祖母有什么价值？’”

w.m: adv. （用于疑问句）在任何时候；曾经

paras.en: As much as many ALifers hate emphasizing their research’s applications, the attempts to create artificial life could have practical payoffs.
paras.zh: 尽管许多ALifer很不愿意强调自己研究的应用，但创造人工生命的尝试有可能带来实际的回报。

paras.en: Artificial intelligence may be considered ALife’s cousin in that researchers in both fields are enamored with a concept called open-ended evolution (演化).
paras.zh: 人工智能或许可以看作ALife的“表亲”，因为这两个领域的研究者都迷恋一个叫作“开放式演化”的概念。

w.m: adj. 开放式的；无限制的

paras.en: This is the capacity for a system to create essentially endless complexity, to be a sort of “novelty generator”.
paras.zh: 这指的是一个系统创造出近乎无穷无尽的复杂性、成为某种“新奇事物生成器”的能力。

paras.en: The only system known to exhibit this is Earth’s biosphere.
paras.zh: 已知唯一能表现出这种能力的系统是地球的生物圈。

paras.en: If the field of ALife manages to reproduce life’s endless “creativity” in some virtual model, those same principles could give rise to truly inventive machines.
paras.zh: 如果ALife领域能够在某个虚拟模型中重现生命无穷无尽的“创造力”，那么同样的原理就可能催生出真正富有创造性的机器。

w.m: adj. 有创造性的；善于创造的

paras.en: Compared with developments in AI, advances in ALife are harder to recognize.
paras.zh: 与人工智能的发展相比，ALife的进展更难辨识。

paras.en: One reason is that ALife is a field in which the central concept — life itself — is undefined.
paras.zh: 原因之一在于，ALife这一领域的核心概念——生命本身——尚无定义。

w.m: adj. 未定义的；不明确的

paras.en: The lack of agreement among ALifers doesn’t help either.
paras.zh: ALifer之间缺乏共识，这也无济于事。

paras.en: The result is a diverse range of projects that each advance along their unique paths.
paras.zh: 结果就是出现了各种各样的项目，每个项目都沿着自己独特的道路推进。

paras.en: For better or worse, ALife mirrors the very subject it studies.
paras.zh: 不论是好是坏，ALife都恰恰映照出它所研究的对象本身。

paras.en: Its muddled (混乱的) progression is a striking parallel (平行线) to the evolutionary struggles that have shaped Earth’s biosphere.
paras.zh: 它混乱的发展历程，与生物演化中塑造了地球生物圈的种种艰难挣扎惊人地相似。

w.m: n. 相似之处；（可相比拟的）对应物

paras.en: Undefined and uncontrolled, ALife drives its followers to repurpose old ideas and generate novelty.
paras.zh: ALife既无定义，又不受控制，这驱使其追随者为旧观念找到新用途，并创造出新奇事物。

w.m: v. 改变……的用途；再利用

paras.en: It may be, of course, that these characteristics aren’t in any way surprising or singular.
paras.zh: 当然，也可能这些特点丝毫不令人惊讶，也并非独一无二。

w.m: 丝毫不；在任何方面都不

paras.en: They may apply universally to all acts of evolution.
paras.zh: 它们可能普遍适用于一切演化活动。

paras.en: Ultimately ALife may be nothing special.
paras.zh: 归根结底，ALife可能并没有什么特别之处。

paras.en: But even this dismissal suggests something: perhaps, just like life itself throughout the universe, the rise of ALife will prove unavoidable.
paras.zh: 但即便是这种否定也说明了一点：或许，就像生命本身在整个宇宙中的兴起一样，ALife的兴起终将被证明是不可避免的。

passages.name: 2023 天津卷（第一次·3月） 阅读C
passages.title: 神经美学：我们如何从艺术中获得愉悦
passages.genre: 说明文 · 艺术与科学
passages.summary: 作者热爱艺术，一直在思考人们如何从艺术中获得愉悦，而神经美学或许能给出答案。研究认为，我们觉得有些艺术美、有些艺术丑，归根结底取决于“审美三元组合”：感觉—运动、情绪—评价和意义—知识。了解这些之后，作者打算今后创作时更加珍视创作过程。

paras.en: I love making art and looking at artworks.
paras.zh: 我热爱创作艺术，也喜欢欣赏艺术作品。

paras.en: I’ve found myself wondering how we gain pleasure from art.
paras.zh: 我发现自己一直在思考：我们是如何从艺术中获得愉悦的？

w.m: 发现自己（不知不觉地）在做……

paras.en: And now neuroaesthetics, a combination of neuroscience (神经科学) and aesthetics (美学), may provide an answer.
paras.zh: 而如今，结合了神经科学与美学的神经美学，或许能给出答案。

paras.en: Neuroaesthetics is a relatively young field of research on what happens in the brain when we make aesthetic assessments.
paras.zh: 神经美学是一个相对年轻的研究领域，研究的是我们进行审美评判时大脑中发生了什么。

paras.en: Researchers use brain imaging techniques to see which brain areas light up when we view paintings that we consider beautiful.
paras.zh: 研究人员借助脑成像技术，观察我们观看自己认为美的画作时，大脑的哪些区域会亮起来。

w.m: 亮起来；（大脑区域）活跃起来

paras.en: Similar research has been done to understand the “neuronal fireworks” that occur when we look at inspiring sculptures, attractive faces, impressive dance, etc.
paras.zh: 为了弄清我们观看鼓舞人心的雕塑、迷人的面孔、令人赞叹的舞蹈等时出现的“神经元烟花”，人们也开展了类似的研究。

w.m: adj. 迷人的；有吸引力的
adj. 令人赞叹的；令人印象深刻的

paras.en: But why do we find some art beautiful and other art ugly?
paras.zh: 但是，为什么我们会觉得有些艺术美、有些艺术丑呢？

paras.en: According to research, it all comes down to the “aesthetic triad (三元组合)”.
paras.zh: 据研究，这一切都归结于“审美三元组合”。

paras.en: The first part of the triad is sensory-motor.
paras.zh: 三元组合的第一部分是感觉—运动。

paras.en: This involves perceiving things like colours, shapes and movements.
paras.zh: 这涉及对颜色、形状和动作等事物的感知。

paras.en: Movement in art has an interesting role.
paras.zh: 艺术中的动作所起的作用很有意思。

paras.en: If you see a painting of a movement, like of a man pulling his arm away after being bitten by a dog, you feel as if you are going through a similar experience.
paras.zh: 如果你看到一幅描绘动作的画，比如一个男人被狗咬后把手臂缩回去，你会感觉自己仿佛也在经历类似的体验。

paras.en: The part of your brain that controls your own movements lights up in response.
paras.zh: 你大脑中控制自身动作的那部分会随之亮起来。

paras.en: Second is emotion-valuation.
paras.zh: 第二部分是情绪—评价。

paras.en: This is how a piece of art makes you feel, and whether or not you appreciate or enjoy that feeling.
paras.zh: 这指的是一件艺术作品给你带来怎样的感受，以及你是否欣赏或享受那种感受。

paras.en: The part of the brain related to pleasure is activated in response to something we find beautiful.
paras.zh: 一遇到我们觉得美的事物，大脑中与愉悦相关的部分就会被激活。

paras.en: This system can be affected in fascinating ways, as found by research using transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) (经颅磁刺激).
paras.zh: 使用经颅磁刺激（TMS）的研究发现，这一系统可能会受到一些奇妙的影响。

w.m: adj. 奇妙的；引人入胜的

paras.en: If TMS is applied to a specific part of your brain behind your forehead that is particularly important for decision-making, you suddenly like different kinds of art.
paras.zh: 如果对你前额后方一个对决策尤为重要的特定大脑区域施加TMS，你喜欢的艺术类型会突然改变。

paras.en: Such stimulation produces significant changes in aesthetic appreciation of faces, bodies and artworks.
paras.zh: 这种刺激会使人们对面孔、身体和艺术作品的审美欣赏发生显著变化。

paras.en: The third part is meaning-knowledge.
paras.zh: 第三部分是意义—知识。

paras.en: This is to do with how we can connect with a piece of art and what meaning we can create in it.
paras.zh: 这关系到我们如何与一件艺术作品建立联系，以及我们能在其中创造出什么意义。

paras.en: Art is deeply personal, because when two people see the same artwork, their perceptions can create vastly different experiences of meaning.
paras.zh: 艺术极具个人色彩，因为两个人看同一件艺术作品时，他们各自的感知可能带来截然不同的意义体验。

paras.en: If we find meaning, then we often find pleasure.
paras.zh: 如果我们找到了意义，往往也就能获得愉悦。

paras.en: We also get enjoyment from the knowledge of how something was made.
paras.zh: 了解某样东西是如何制作出来的，也会给我们带来乐趣。

paras.en: For the images that an artist creates, viewers will probably get far more enjoyment once they know the process used to create them.
paras.zh: 就艺术家创作的画面而言，观众一旦了解了创作这些画面的过程，很可能会获得多得多的乐趣。

paras.en: Informed by neuroaesthetics, the next time I create my art I will value the process even more, enjoying the activation of the aesthetic triad in my brain as I admire the vivid images that I have created.
paras.zh: 了解了神经美学之后，下次进行艺术创作时，我会更加珍视创作过程，一边欣赏自己创作出的生动画面，一边享受大脑中审美三元组合被激活的感觉。

w.m: v. 使了解；为……提供依据

passages.name: 2023 天津卷（第一次·3月） 阅读D
passages.title: 故意犯错效应的妙用
passages.genre: 议论文 · 学习与成长
passages.summary: 大多数人认同应从意外的失败中吸取教训，却很少有人提倡故意犯错。文章介绍了“故意犯错效应”：在新加坡国立大学的一项实验中，先故意在术语描述中加入错误再改正的参与者，学到的东西大约是只照抄正确定义者的两倍。作者认为，这一效应还可用于音乐、烹饪、绘画等方面：最坏也能重温并加深对规则的了解，最好则可能带来全新的、意想不到的发现。

paras.en: Most people with good sense would accept that we can and should learn from accidental failures.
paras.zh: 大多数明智的人都会认同：我们能够而且应该从意外的失败中吸取教训。

paras.en: It would be impossible to progress in anything, after all, without taking the occasional misstep.
paras.zh: 毕竟，不偶尔出点失误，做任何事都不可能取得进步。

paras.en: And by understanding how we slipped, we can avoid falling in the future.
paras.zh: 而弄清自己是怎样滑倒的，我们将来就能避免摔倒。

paras.en: Few would advocate making intentional mistakes, however.
paras.zh: 然而，很少有人会提倡故意犯错。

paras.en: Yet consciously erring (犯错) can promote deeper understanding and better recall.
paras.zh: 但有意识地犯错能促进更深入的理解，增强记忆。

paras.en: The phenomenon is known as the derring effect—coming from “deliberate (故意的) erring”—and when applied properly, it may bring benefits in many unexpected areas of life.
paras.zh: 这种现象被称为“故意犯错效应”（derring effect），名称源自“deliberate erring”（故意犯错）；如果运用得当，它可能在生活中许多意想不到的领域带来好处。

paras.en: In one experiment carried out at the National University of Singapore, participants were given the task of learning concepts on a difficult subject.
paras.zh: 在新加坡国立大学开展的一项实验中，参与者接到的任务是学习一门较难学科中的一些概念。

paras.en: For some terms, they simply copied out the correct definition; for others, they were asked to first add an error in their description of the term before correcting the mistake.
paras.zh: 对于一部分术语，他们只是照抄正确的定义；对于另一部分术语，他们被要求先在对术语的描述中加入一个错误，然后再改正这个错误。

paras.en: Naturally, you would expect the addition of the errors to have increased unwanted confusion.
paras.zh: 按常理，你会以为加入错误会增加不必要的困惑。

paras.en: Yet the exact opposite was true: the participants who made deliberate errors learned about twice as much as the people who simply copied out the correct definitions.
paras.zh: 然而事实恰恰相反：故意犯错的参与者学到的东西，大约是只照抄正确定义的人的两倍。

paras.en: The derring effect could be applied in other situations.
paras.zh: 故意犯错效应还可以应用于其他情境。

paras.en: So a music teacher may find the addition of deliberate errors could help a student remember the right musical notes.
paras.zh: 比如，音乐老师可能会发现，故意加入一些错误能帮助学生记住正确的音符。

paras.en: Such a playful approach could fuel their creativity for composition, if the student looks for ways to develop those wrong notes into something more attractive.
paras.zh: 如果学生设法把那些错误的音符发展成更动听的东西，这种好玩的方法就可能激发学生的作曲创造力。

w.m: adj. 有吸引力的；动听的

paras.en: It is encouraging to discover that by readily accepting our errors and wisely placing ourselves in the way of being wrong, we can in fact overcome weaknesses and rise stronger.
paras.zh: 令人鼓舞的是，我们发现，通过欣然接受自己的错误、明智地让自己置身于可能出错的境地，其实就能克服弱点，重新站起来，变得更强。

w.h: place oneself in the way of
w.m: 使自己置身于（可能遇到……的）境地

paras.en: The derring effect could be useful for many other challenges too.
paras.zh: 故意犯错效应也可能有助于应对其他许多挑战。

paras.en: If you enjoy cooking, for example, you may faithfully follow a recipe without questioning the instructions.
paras.zh: 比如，如果你喜欢做饭，你可能会严格地照着菜谱做，而不去质疑其中的说明。

paras.en: But why not try to break away from those habits and deliberately do the “wrong” thing for a change, and see where your derring takes you?
paras.zh: 可为什么不试着摆脱这些习惯，换换花样，故意做些“错”事，看看这样故意犯错会把你带向何方呢？

w.m: 换换花样；为了改变一下

paras.en: If you are painting, meanwhile, you could relax one of the constraints (限制) that you usually put on your work and see what you produce.
paras.zh: 而如果你在画画，可以把平时给自己作品设下的限制放宽一条，看看会画出些什么。

paras.en: At worst, you will have refreshed and deepened your knowledge of the rules you normally apply, so that you can be even more effective next time.
paras.zh: 往最坏处说，你也能重温自己平时所遵循的规则，并加深对它们的了解，这样下次就能更有成效。

paras.en: At best, you may just find that you have discovered something completely new and unexpected, through a flash of inspiration that you would have missed with perfectionism.
paras.zh: 往最好处说，你说不定会借着灵光一闪，发现某种全新的、意想不到的东西；而如果抱着完美主义，你就会错过这一闪而过的灵感。

paras.en: Either way, your apparent missteps will have moved you a little closer to true mastery.
paras.zh: 无论哪种情况，你那些看似失误的举动，都会让你离真正的精通更近一点。

passages.name: 2023 天津卷（第二次·6月） 阅读C
passages.title: 狗或许能读懂人的意图
passages.genre: 说明文 · 动物与科学
passages.summary: 新研究表明，狗可能具备曾被认为是人类独有的“心理理论”。2023年的一项研究发现，与“不愿意”情境相比，在实验者“无法”把零食递过去之后，狗更有耐心，眼神交流也更多；2021年的一项类似研究也发现，狗在“无法”情境中明显更早地走近实验者，但2023年那项研究的研究人员认为，这一结果可能受到了掉落在地上的食物的影响。狗究竟如何获得解读意图的能力，将是未来研究的课题。

paras.en: Getting the “side-eye” look from your dog can make it seem like they are making a judgement about you, and some new studies suggest they really could be.
paras.zh: 自家狗狗“斜眼”看你时，你可能会觉得它好像在评判你，而一些新研究表明，它或许真的是在评判你。

w.m: n. 斜眼一瞥（表示怀疑、不满的眼神）

paras.en: The ability to judge others’ intentions is an indicator of possessing “theory of mind”, which was once thought to be unique to humans.
paras.zh: 能够判断他人的意图，是具备“心理理论”的一个标志，而心理理论一度被认为是人类所独有的。

w.m: 心理理论（理解他人心理状态的能力）

paras.en: However, new studies have shown that dogs can read human behaviour and have a preference for people who are more friendly or generous with food.
paras.zh: 然而，新研究表明，狗能够读懂人的行为，而且偏爱更友善或给吃的更大方的人。

paras.en: One such study published in 2023 aimed to see if dogs can tell the difference between humans who are “unwilling” and those who are “unable” to give them a treat.
paras.zh: 2023年发表的一项此类研究旨在弄清，狗能否区分“不愿意”给它们零食的人和“无法”给它们零食的人。

w.m: n. 零食；（给动物的）奖励食物

paras.en: Ninety-six dogs were involved in both “unwilling” and “unable” scenarios (情境) designed for the study.
paras.zh: 96只狗都参与了为这项研究设计的“不愿意”和“无法”两种情境的测试。

paras.en: Both scenarios involved a dog being placed on one side of a glass screen with small holes in it at nose-height, and an experimenter standing on the other.
paras.zh: 两种情境都是把一只狗安置在一块玻璃隔板的一侧，隔板上与狗鼻子齐高的位置开有一些小孔，一名实验者则站在隔板的另一侧。

paras.en: In the “unwilling” scenario, the experimenter would hang a piece of sausage in front of the screen in a “teasing” (戏耍的) manner, and approach one of the holes.
paras.zh: 在“不愿意”情境中，实验者会以“戏耍”的方式把一块香肠悬在隔板前，并靠近其中一个小孔。

paras.en: But instead of passing it through the hole to the dog, they would then pull it out of the dog’s reach.
paras.zh: 但实验者随后并没有把香肠从孔中递给狗，而是把它拿开，让狗够不着。

paras.en: For the “unable” scenario, the experimenter would again move the treat towards the hole while the dog watched, but “accidentally” drop it before they could pass it through.
paras.zh: 在“无法”情境中，实验者同样会在狗的注视下把零食移向小孔，但在递过去之前“不小心”让它掉了下去。

paras.en: The researchers observed that the dogs were much more patient, making more eye contact and staying closer to the screen after the “unable” scenario played out.
paras.zh: 研究人员观察到，“无法”情境结束后，狗要耐心得多：眼神交流更多，也待得离隔板更近。

paras.en: In the “unwilling” scenario, however, the dogs looked at the experimenter less often and sat, lay down and wandered around more frequently.
paras.zh: 然而在“不愿意”情境中，狗看实验者的次数更少，而坐下、趴下和四处走动则更频繁。

paras.en: Another study from 2021 tested for “theory of mind” in dogs in a similar way, but the dogs were able to walk round the screen to obtain the treat after witnessing the experimenter’s “unwilling” or “unable” behaviour.
paras.zh: 2021年的另一项研究以类似的方式检测狗是否具备“心理理论”，不过在这项研究中，狗在目睹实验者“不愿意”或“无法”的行为之后，可以绕过隔板去拿零食。

paras.en: The main finding was that the dogs approached the experimenter significantly sooner in the unable scenario than in the unwilling scenario.
paras.zh: 主要发现是：与“不愿意”情境相比，狗在“无法”情境中明显更早地走近实验者。

paras.en: However, the researchers of the 2023 study argued that the food dropped on the floor in the clumsy (笨拙的) manner might have motivated the dogs to approach the experimenter, considering that they probably often obtain food dropped on the floor in their daily lives.
paras.zh: 不过，2023年那项研究的研究人员认为，考虑到狗在日常生活中很可能常常能吃到掉在地上的食物，实验者笨手笨脚弄掉在地上的食物可能是促使狗走近实验者的原因。

paras.en: Now, more evidence has been provided that dogs distinguish between similar actions associated with different intentions.
paras.zh: 如今，已有更多证据表明，狗会区分与不同意图相关的相似行为。

paras.en: But how exactly they acquire such intention-reading abilities will be an exciting topic for future research.
paras.zh: 但狗究竟是如何获得这种解读意图的能力的，将会是未来研究中一个令人兴奋的课题。

passages.name: 2023 天津卷（第二次·6月） 阅读D
passages.title: 讲故事：学习与理解他人的途径
passages.genre: 说明文 · 语言与文化
passages.summary: 讲故事是一种古老的艺术形式，它不只是娱乐，也是一种学习方式：好故事能调动我们的好奇心、情感和想象力，而且容易记住；研究发现，从讲得好的故事中学到的东西比从事实和数据中学到的记得更准确、更长久。故事还能让我们用不同的视角看待世界；听别人讲亲身经历、设身处地看世界，能激发我们对他人的共情。

paras.en: Storytelling is an ancient art form that has been used to hand down legends, tales and factual stories.
paras.zh: 讲故事是一种古老的艺术形式，人们一直借助它来传承传说、民间故事和真实故事。

w.m: adj. 基于事实的；纪实的

paras.en: Perhaps the first thing that springs to mind when you think of storytelling is the fantasy land that took shape in your mind while Mom or Dad told you stories about princes, castles and monsters, with a unique voice for each character.
paras.zh: 说起讲故事，你首先想到的也许是这样一片奇幻天地：妈妈或爸爸给你讲王子、城堡和怪物的故事，为每个角色配上独特的声音，而那片天地就在你的脑海中渐渐成形。

paras.en: Storytelling does not just take place at bedtime or round a campfire, however.
paras.zh: 不过，讲故事并不只发生在睡前或篝火旁。

paras.en: It can take some other forms, either via the books we read or the films we watch.
paras.zh: 它还可以采取其他一些形式，或是借助我们读的书，或是借助我们看的电影。

paras.en: But they usually have some elements in common: rather than a list of dry facts, stories have plots and they introduce characters.
paras.zh: 但它们通常有一些共同的要素：故事不是罗列一串枯燥的事实，而是有情节，还会引入人物。

paras.en: We respond to stories, particularly when there is emotional detail.
paras.zh: 我们会被故事打动，尤其是在故事中有情感细节的时候。

w.m: 对……作出反应；（情感上）被……打动

paras.en: And contrary to what we may suppose, storytelling is not just a form of entertainment, but a form of learning as well.
paras.zh: 而且，与我们可能以为的不同，讲故事不仅是一种娱乐形式，也是一种学习形式。

paras.en: Long before reading and writing became widely spread and available, oral storytelling had already been a form through which the wisdom and knowledge of the people were passed down from elders to children.
paras.zh: 早在阅读和写作广泛传播、普遍可及之前，口头讲故事就已经是一种传承方式，人们的智慧和知识借此由长辈传给孩子。

w.m: v. 传播；普及（此处为过去分词作表语：流传开的）
adj. 可获得的；可利用的

paras.en: A good story engages our curiosity, emotions and imagination.
paras.zh: 一个好故事能调动我们的好奇心、情感和想象力。

w.m: v. 吸引；调动（兴趣、情感等）

paras.en: Storytelling helps with learning also because stories are easy to remember.
paras.zh: 讲故事之所以有助于学习，还因为故事容易记住。

paras.en: Research has found that learning obtained from a well-told story is remembered more accurately, and for far longer, than from facts and figures.
paras.zh: 研究发现，与从事实和数据中学到的东西相比，从一个讲得好的故事中获得的知识会记得更准确，记住的时间也要长得多。

paras.en: And above all, stories have a transformative power to allow us to see the world in a different way than we do if we just encounter it on our own.
paras.zh: 而最重要的是，故事有一种改变人的力量，能让我们以不同于仅凭自己接触世界时的眼光来看待世界。

paras.en: Stories are an entry point to understanding a different experience of the world.
paras.zh: 故事是一个切入点，让我们得以理解对世界的另一种体验。

paras.en: This aspect of storytelling—presenting a different perspective on the world—is important when it comes to connecting with each other.
paras.zh: 讲故事的这一方面——呈现看待世界的不同视角——在人与人建立联系时非常重要。

paras.en: It gives us an opportunity to learn from another person’s experience and it can shape, strengthen or challenge our opinions and values.
paras.zh: 它让我们有机会从别人的经历中学习，还能塑造、强化或挑战我们的观点和价值观。

paras.en: So, when someone tells us their own personal story, we catch a glimpse (瞥见) of a view of the world that may be slightly or significantly different from our own.
paras.zh: 所以，有人给我们讲自己的亲身经历时，我们就能瞥见一种看待世界的视角，它与我们自己的视角可能略有不同，也可能大不相同。

paras.en: When we see the world as they see it, or walk in their shoes, the experience can inspire empathy (共情；同理心) with them.
paras.zh: 我们像对方那样看待世界，或者站在对方的立场上时，这种体验能激发我们对对方的共情。

w.m: 设身处地；站在别人的立场上

passages.name: 2023 上海卷（春考） 阅读C
passages.title: 化石：判断岩石年代的依据
passages.genre: 说明文 · 地质与古生物
passages.summary: 科学家通过研究层状岩石中的化石来判断岩石的年代。恐龙虽广受关注，但只占地球物种的一小部分，化石记录的绝大部分是有壳动物的化石和动植物的微体遗存。18世纪末至19世纪初，威廉·史密斯等人发现同一年代的岩石可能含有相同的化石；史密斯还把这一知识用于修建运河。化石所保存的生命形式演替顺序有助于了解岩石如何、何时形成，而解释这一演替的理论直到后来才出现。

paras.en: To tell the age of most layered rocks, scientists study the fossils these rocks contain.
paras.zh: 要判断大多数层状岩石的年代，科学家会研究这些岩石中所含的化石。

paras.en: Fossils provide important evidence to help determine what happened in Earth history and when it happened.
paras.zh: 化石提供了重要证据，有助于确定地球历史上发生过什么以及发生在何时。

paras.en: The word “fossil” makes many people think of dinosaurs.
paras.zh: “化石”这个词让许多人想到恐龙。

paras.en: Dinosaurs are now featured in books, movies, and television programs, and the bones of some large dinosaurs are on display in many museums.
paras.zh: 如今，恐龙出现在书籍、电影和电视节目中，一些大型恐龙的骨骼还在许多博物馆里展出。

w.m: v. 以……为主要内容；使出现（在书、电影等中）

paras.en: These reptiles were dominant animals on Earth for well over 100 million years from the Late Triassic through the Late Cretaceous.
paras.zh: 从三叠纪晚期到白垩纪晚期，在远超1亿年的时间里，这些爬行动物一直是地球上的优势动物。

w.m: adj. 占优势的；占主导地位的

paras.en: Many dinosaurs were quite small, but by the middle of the Mesozoic Era, some species weighed as much as 80 tons.
paras.zh: 许多恐龙体型相当小，但到了中生代中期，有些物种的体重达80吨之多。

paras.en: By around 65 million years ago all dinosaurs were extinct.
paras.zh: 到大约6500万年前，所有恐龙都已灭绝。

paras.en: In spite of all of the interest in dinosaurs, they form only a small fraction of the millions of species that live and have lived on Earth.
paras.zh: 尽管人们对恐龙兴趣浓厚，但在地球上现存和曾经存在过的数百万个物种中，恐龙只占很小一部分。

paras.en: The great bulk of the fossil record is dominated by fossils of animals with shells and microscopic remains of plants and animals, and these remains are widespread in sedimentary rocks.
paras.zh: 化石记录的绝大部分是有壳动物的化石和动植物的微体遗存，这些遗存广泛分布于沉积岩中。

w.m: v. 在……中占主导地位；支配
adj. 微小的；需用显微镜才能看见的

paras.en: It is these fossils that are studied by most paleontologists.
paras.zh: 大多数古生物学家研究的正是这些化石。

paras.en: In the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, the English geologist and engineer William Smith and the French paleontologists Georges Cuvier and Alexandre Brongniart discovered that rocks of the same age may contain the same fossils even when the rocks are separated by long distances.
paras.zh: 18世纪末和19世纪初，英国地质学家兼工程师威廉·史密斯以及法国古生物学家乔治·居维叶和亚历山大·布隆尼亚尔发现，即使相隔遥远，同一年代的岩石也可能含有相同的化石。

paras.en: They published the first geologic maps of large areas on which rocks containing similar fossils were shown.
paras.zh: 他们出版了首批覆盖大片区域的地质图，图上标出了含有相似化石的岩石。

paras.en: By careful observation of the rocks and their fossils, these men and other geologists were able to recognize rocks of the same age on opposite sides of the English Channel.
paras.zh: 通过仔细观察岩石及其所含化石，这些人和其他地质学家得以辨认出英吉利海峡两岸同一年代的岩石。

paras.en: William Smith was able to apply his knowledge of fossils in a very practical way.
paras.zh: 威廉·史密斯得以把自己的化石知识运用到非常实际的用途上。

paras.en: He was an engineer building canals in England, which has lots of vegetation and few surface exposures of rock.
paras.zh: 他是在英格兰修建运河的工程师，而英格兰植被茂盛，地表很少有裸露的岩石。

paras.en: He needed to know what rocks he could expect to find on the hills through which he had to build a canal.
paras.zh: 他需要知道，在运河必须穿过的那些山丘上，自己预计会找到哪些岩石。

paras.en: Often he could tell what kind of rock was likely to be below the surface by examining the fossils that had eroded from the rocks of the hillside or by digging a small hole to find fossils.
paras.zh: 他查看从山坡岩石上侵蚀脱落的化石，或者挖个小洞找化石，往往就能判断出地表以下可能是哪种岩石。

w.m: v. 侵蚀；（因侵蚀而）脱落

paras.en: Knowing what rocks to expect allowed Smith to estimate costs and determine what tools were needed for the job.
paras.zh: 知道会遇到哪些岩石，史密斯就能估算成本，并确定这项工程需要哪些工具。

paras.en: Smith and others knew that the succession of life forms preserved as fossils is useful for understanding how and when the rocks formed.
paras.zh: 史密斯等人知道，保存为化石的各种生命形式，其演替顺序有助于了解这些岩石如何形成、何时形成。

w.m: n. 演替；连续的一系列

paras.en: Only later did scientists develop a theory to explain that succession.
paras.zh: 直到后来，科学家们才提出了解释这种演替顺序的理论。

passages.name: 2023 上海卷（秋考） 阅读C
passages.title: 宇宙膨胀速度之谜
passages.genre: 说明文 · 天文与科学探索
passages.summary: 哈勃望远镜测得的当今宇宙膨胀速度，比根据普朗克卫星对早期宇宙的观测所预期的更快。哈勃的最新数据把这一差异纯属统计巧合的可能性降到十万分之一，为“可能需要新的物理学来调和这种不一致”的假说提供了支持。研究人员借助造父变星校准“宇宙距离阶梯”，把哈勃常数的不确定度降到1.9%，但结果仍与普朗克卫星的观测所预测的数值不符。

paras.en: The universe expands with every passing second, stretching the space between galaxies like dough rising in an oven.
paras.zh: 宇宙每过一秒都在膨胀，把星系之间的空间不断拉大，就像烤箱里正在发起来的面团一样。

paras.en: But just how fast is this expansion happening?
paras.zh: 但这种膨胀到底有多快呢？

paras.en: As telescopes like Hubble strive to answer this fundamental question, they encounter a perplexing gap between theoretical predictions and observed data.
paras.zh: 哈勃等望远镜在努力回答这个基本问题的过程中，遇到了理论预测与观测数据之间令人费解的差距。

paras.en: Hubble’s measurements indicate a faster rate of expansion in the modern universe than was expected based on the European Space Agency’s Planck satellite observations of the universe as it was more than 13 billion years ago.
paras.zh: 哈勃望远镜的测量结果表明，当今宇宙的膨胀速度比预期的更快；而这一预期是根据欧洲航天局普朗克卫星对130多亿年前宇宙的观测得出的。

paras.en: This inconsistency has been a subject of scientific inquiry for several years.
paras.zh: 几年来，这种不一致一直是科学研究的一个课题。

paras.en: However, it remains uncertain whether differences in measurement techniques or chance variations are responsible for this disparity.
paras.zh: 然而，造成这种差异的究竟是测量技术的不同，还是偶然的波动，目前仍不确定。

paras.en: Recent data from the Hubble telescope have significantly reduced the possibility that this discrepancy is merely a statistical fluke, with the chances now estimated at only 1 in 100,000.
paras.zh: 哈勃望远镜的最新数据大大降低了这一偏差纯属统计巧合的可能性，目前估计这种可能性仅为十万分之一。

paras.en: This marks a substantial improvement from previous estimates, which placed the odds at 1 in 3,000 less than a year ago.
paras.zh: 这比此前的估计有了很大进步：不到一年前，对这一概率的估计还是三千分之一。

paras.en: These precise measurements from Hubble lend weight to the hypothesis that new physics may be necessary to reconcile the observed mismatch.
paras.zh: 哈勃望远镜的这些精确测量结果为一种假说增添了分量：可能需要新的物理学，才能调和观测到的这种不一致。

paras.en: Lead researcher Adam Riess, a Nobel laureate from the Space Telescope Science Institute and Johns Hopkins University, describes the tension between the early and late universe as one of the most exciting developments in cosmology in decades.
paras.zh: 首席研究员亚当·里斯是来自空间望远镜科学研究所和约翰斯·霍普金斯大学的诺贝尔奖得主，他把早期宇宙与晚期宇宙之间的这种矛盾形容为几十年来宇宙学领域最激动人心的进展之一。

paras.en: He emphasizes that the growing disparity cannot be dismissed as a random occurrence and suggests that it may signal the need for a deeper understanding of the cosmos.
paras.zh: 他强调，日益扩大的差异不能当作随机事件而不予理会，并认为这可能意味着需要更深入地认识宇宙。

paras.en: To determine distances in the universe, scientists rely on a “cosmic distance ladder” method.
paras.zh: 为了测定宇宙中的距离，科学家们依靠一种“宇宙距离阶梯”方法。

paras.en: This involves accurately measuring distances to nearby galaxies and then using progressively more distant galaxies as reference points.
paras.zh: 这种方法先精确测量到邻近星系的距离，再逐步以更远的星系作为参照点。

paras.en: By observing stars like Cepheid variables, astronomers can calibrate this distance ladder.
paras.zh: 通过观测造父变星这样的恒星，天文学家可以校准这一距离阶梯。

paras.en: Riess and his team have been refining these measurements since 2005, aiming to improve our understanding of cosmic distances.
paras.zh: 自2005年以来，里斯和他的团队一直在改进这些测量，旨在增进我们对宇宙距离的认识。

paras.en: In their latest study, astronomers used Hubble to observe 70 Cepheid variables in the Large Magellanic Cloud.
paras.zh: 在最新的研究中，天文学家利用哈勃望远镜观测了大麦哲伦云中的70颗造父变星。

paras.en: By comparing these stars with their more distant counterparts in galaxies hosting supernovae, they refined their measurement of the Hubble constant, reducing its uncertainty from 2.2% to 1.9%.
paras.zh: 通过把这些恒星与存在超新星的星系中更遥远的同类恒星进行比较，他们改进了对哈勃常数的测量，将其不确定度从2.2%降到了1.9%。

w.m: n. 不确定性；不确定度

paras.en: Despite this increased precision, their calculated Hubble constant remains at odds with the value predicted by observations of the early universe conducted by Planck.
paras.zh: 尽管精确度提高了，他们计算出的哈勃常数仍与根据普朗克卫星对早期宇宙的观测所预测的数值不符。

paras.en: The Planck satellite, which mapped the cosmic microwave background – a remnant of the universe’s early stages – provides crucial data for understanding the universe’s expansion.
paras.zh: 宇宙微波背景是宇宙早期阶段的遗迹，普朗克卫星绘制了它的分布图，为理解宇宙的膨胀提供了至关重要的数据。

w.m: v. 绘制……的（分布）图；测绘

paras.en: However, the discrepancy between these measurements and those from Hubble underscores the need for further investigation and the potential for new discoveries in cosmology.
paras.zh: 然而，普朗克卫星的这些测量结果与哈勃望远镜的测量结果之间的差异，凸显了进一步研究的必要性，也表明宇宙学领域有可能出现新的发现。

passages.name: 2023 浙江卷（1月） 阅读C
passages.title: 人与机器之别在于“意义”
passages.genre: 议论文 · 人工智能与人类
passages.summary: 名为 Project Debater 的软件程序在一场公开辩论中击败了人类对手，但它是从资料库中提取句子再串联起来的；正如一位教授所说，这个系统从来不知道自己在说什么。作者指出，计算机按规则处理符号，却不理会符号的意义；对人类而言，意义却是一切，它在社会互动中产生，赋予意义的规则也存在于社会之中，这正是人与机器的区别所在。因此，无论 Project Debater 看起来多么惊人，始于苏格拉底和孔子的传统都不会终结于人工智能。

paras.en: A machine can now not only beat you at chess but also outperform you in debate.
paras.zh: 如今，机器不仅能在国际象棋上打败你，还能在辩论中胜过你。

paras.en: Last week, in a public debate in San Francisco, a software program called Project Debater beat its human opponents, including Noa Ovadia, Israel’s former national debating champion.
paras.zh: 上周，在旧金山举行的一场公开辩论中，一个名为 Project Debater 的软件程序击败了人类对手，其中包括以色列前全国辩论冠军诺阿·奥瓦迪亚。

paras.en: Brilliant though it is, Project Debater has some weaknesses.
paras.zh: Project Debater 虽然很出色，却也有一些弱点。

w.m: adj. 出色的；才华横溢的
conj. 虽然（用于“形容词＋though＋主语＋谓语”的让步倒装）

paras.en: It takes sentences from its library of documents and prebuilt arguments and strings them together.
paras.zh: 它的资料库里存有文档和预先构建好的论点，它从中提取句子，再把这些句子串在一起。

paras.en: This can lead to the kinds of errors no human would make.
paras.zh: 这可能导致一些人类绝不会犯的错误。

paras.en: Such wrinkles will no doubt be ironed out, yet they also point to a fundamental problem.
paras.zh: 这类小毛病无疑会被消除，但它们也暴露出一个根本性的问题。

paras.en: As Kristian Hammond, professor of electrical engineering and computer science at Northwestern University, put it: “There’s never a stage at which the system knows what it’s talking about.”
paras.zh: 正如美国西北大学电气工程与计算机科学教授克里斯蒂安·哈蒙德所说：“这个系统在任何阶段都不知道自己在说什么。”

w.m: 说；表达（as sb. put it 正如某人所说）

paras.en: What Hammond is referring to is the question of meaning, and meaning is central to what distinguishes the least intelligent of humans from the most intelligent of machines.
paras.zh: 哈蒙德所说的是意义问题，而意义正是区分最不聪明的人与最聪明的机器的核心所在。

paras.en: A computer works with symbols.
paras.zh: 计算机处理的是符号。

paras.en: Its program specifies a set of rules to transform one string of symbols into another.
paras.zh: 它的程序规定了一套规则，把一串符号转换成另一串符号。

paras.en: But it does not specify what those symbols mean.
paras.zh: 但程序并不规定这些符号是什么意思。

paras.en: Indeed, to a computer, meaning is irrelevant.
paras.zh: 事实上，对计算机来说，意义无关紧要。

w.m: adj. 无关紧要的；不相关的

paras.en: Humans, in thinking, talking, reading and writing, also work with symbols.
paras.zh: 人类在思考、谈话、阅读和写作时，也要处理符号。

paras.en: But for humans, meaning is everything.
paras.zh: 但对人类来说，意义就是一切。

paras.en: When we communicate, we communicate meaning.
paras.zh: 我们交流时，交流的是意义。

paras.en: What matters is not just the outside of a string of symbols, but the inside too, not just how they are arranged but what they mean.
paras.zh: 重要的不只是一串符号的外表，还有其内里；不只是符号如何排列，还有它们是什么意思。

paras.en: Meaning emerges through a process of social interaction, not of computation, interaction that shapes the content of the symbols in our heads.
paras.zh: 意义产生于社会互动的过程，而非计算的过程，正是这种互动塑造了我们头脑中符号的内容。

paras.en: The rules that assign meaning lie not just inside our heads, but also outside, in society, in social memory, social conventions and social relations.
paras.zh: 赋予意义的规则不仅存在于我们的头脑之中，也存在于头脑之外，存在于社会之中，存在于社会记忆、社会习俗和社会关系之中。

paras.en: It is this that distinguishes humans from machines.
paras.zh: 正是这一点把人类与机器区分开来。

paras.en: And that’s why, however astonishing Project Debater may seem, the tradition that began with Socrates and Confucius will not end with artificial intelligence.
paras.zh: 正因如此，无论 Project Debater 看起来多么惊人，始于苏格拉底和孔子的传统都不会终结于人工智能。

w.m: 这就是……的原因；正因如此

passages.name: 2023 浙江卷（1月） 阅读D
passages.title: 太阳能电站为传粉昆虫安家
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与环保
passages.summary: 过去十年，已安装的太阳能电池板数量增长迅速，但开发商常在电池板下铺满小石子、用化学药剂控制杂草，结果许多社区把太阳能电站看作土壤的破坏者。InSPIRE 项目正在研究对土地更友好的“低影响”太阳能开发方法，其中最简单的方法之一是为传粉昆虫提供栖息地。过去几年，许多开发商已把电池板下方的空间改造成传粉昆虫的庇护所，从而改善了土壤，减少了碳排放。

paras.en: According to the Solar Energy Industries Association, the number of solar panels installed (安装) has grown rapidly in the past decade, and it has to grow even faster to meet climate goals.
paras.zh: 据太阳能产业协会称，过去十年里，已安装的太阳能电池板数量增长迅速，而要实现气候目标，增长速度还必须更快。

w.m: v. 达到；满足（目标、要求）

paras.en: But all of that growth will take up a lot of space, and though more and more people accept the concept of solar energy, few like large solar panels to be installed near them.
paras.zh: 但所有这些增长都会占用大量空间；而且，尽管越来越多的人接受了太阳能这一理念，却很少有人愿意自家附近装上大型太阳能电池板。

w.m: pron. 很少的人；几乎没人

paras.en: Solar developers want to put up panels as quickly and cheaply as possible, so they haven’t given much thought to what they put under them.
paras.zh: 太阳能开发商希望尽可能快速、低成本地架设电池板，因此一直没怎么考虑在电池板下面放些什么。

paras.en: Often, they’ll end up filling the area with small stones and using chemicals to control weeds.
paras.zh: 他们最后往往会在这片区域铺满小石子，并使用化学药剂来控制杂草。

paras.en: The result is that many communities, especially in farming regions, see solar farms as destroyers of the soil.
paras.zh: 结果，许多社区，尤其是农业地区的社区，都把太阳能电站看作土壤的破坏者。

w.m: 太阳能电站；太阳能发电场

paras.en: “Solar projects need to be good neighbors,” says Jordan Macknick, the head of the Innovative Site Preparation and Impact Reductions on the Environment (InSPIRE) project.
paras.zh: “创新场地准备与降低环境影响”（InSPIRE）项目负责人乔丹·麦克尼克说：“太阳能项目需要做个好邻居。”

paras.en: “They need to be protectors of the land and contribute to the agricultural economy.”
paras.zh: “它们需要成为土地的保护者，并为农业经济做出贡献。”

paras.en: InSPIRE is investigating practical approaches to “low-impact” solar development, which focuses on establishing and operating solar farms in a way that is kinder to the land.
paras.zh: InSPIRE 项目正在研究实现“低影响”太阳能开发的可行方法，这种开发注重以对土地更友好的方式建设和运营太阳能电站。

w.m: adj. 切实可行的；实用的
adj. 低影响的；对环境影响小的

paras.en: One of the easiest low-impact solar strategies is providing habitat for pollinators (传粉昆虫).
paras.zh: 最简单的低影响太阳能策略之一，就是为传粉昆虫提供栖息地。

paras.en: Habitat loss, pesticide use, and climate change have caused dramatic declines in pollinator populations over the past couple of decades, which has damaged the U.S. agricultural economy.
paras.zh: 过去二十来年里，栖息地丧失、农药使用和气候变化导致传粉昆虫数量急剧下降，这已经损害了美国的农业经济。

paras.en: Over 28 states have passed laws related to pollinator habitat protection and pesticide use.
paras.zh: 已有超过28个州通过了与传粉昆虫栖息地保护和农药使用相关的法律。

paras.en: Conservation organizations put out pollinator-friendliness guidelines for home gardens, businesses, schools, cities—and now there are guidelines for solar farms.
paras.zh: 各类自然保护组织针对家庭花园、企业、学校和城市发布了如何善待传粉昆虫的指南，如今也有了针对太阳能电站的同类指南。

paras.en: Over the past few years, many solar farm developers have transformed the space under their solar panels into a shelter for various kinds of pollinators, resulting in soil improvement and carbon reduction.
paras.zh: 过去几年里，许多太阳能电站开发商已把电池板下方的空间改造成各类传粉昆虫的庇护所，从而改善了土壤，减少了碳排放。

paras.en: “These pollinator-friendly solar farms can have a valuable impact on everything that’s going on in the landscape,” says Macknick.
paras.zh: “这些对传粉昆虫友好的太阳能电站，能给这一带土地上正在发生的一切带来非常有益的影响，”麦克尼克说。

w.m: adj. 对传粉昆虫友好的

passages.name: 2024 全国新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读C
passages.title: 纸质阅读与数字阅读的效果差异
passages.genre: 说明文 · 教育与学习
passages.summary: 读屏幕和读纸张的理解效果往往并不相同；听和看也往往不如阅读文字有效，原因涉及注意力下降、娱乐心态和一心多用的倾向等。大量研究表明，阅读较长文本时，纸质阅读的学习效果通常更好，这在一定程度上与纸张的实体特性有关，也与“浅层化假说”所描述的心理因素有关。作者认为数字文本、音频和视频都有教育作用，但在需要专注和反思的学习中，教育者不应认为各种媒介效果相同。

paras.en: Is comprehension the same whether a person reads a text onscreen or on paper?
paras.zh: 一个人无论是在屏幕上还是在纸上阅读文本，理解程度都一样吗？

paras.en: And are listening to and viewing content as effective as reading the written word when covering the same material?
paras.zh: 而在所涉材料相同的情况下，收听和观看内容是否与阅读书面文字一样有效？

paras.en: The answers to both questions are often “no”.
paras.zh: 这两个问题的答案往往都是否定的。

paras.en: The reasons relate to a variety of factors, including reduced concentration, an entertainment mindset (心态) and a tendency to multitask while consuming digital content.
paras.zh: 其原因与多种因素有关，包括注意力下降、娱乐心态，以及在接收数字内容时一心多用的倾向。

w.m: v. 同时处理多项任务；一心多用
v. 接收（信息、内容）；消费

paras.en: When people read texts of several hundred words or more, learning is generally more successful when it’s on paper than onscreen.
paras.zh: 当人们阅读几百个词或更长的文本时，纸质阅读的学习效果通常比屏幕阅读更好。

paras.en: A large amount of research confirms this finding.
paras.zh: 大量研究证实了这一发现。

paras.en: The benefits of print reading particularly shine through when experimenters move from posing simple tasks — like identifying the main idea in a reading passage — to ones that require mental abstraction — such as drawing inferences from a text.
paras.zh: 当实验者不再布置简单任务（比如找出一篇阅读文章的主旨），而是转向布置需要抽象思维的任务（比如从文本中作出推断）时，纸质阅读的优势就格外明显。

paras.en: The differences between print and digital reading results are partly related to paper’s physical properties.
paras.zh: 纸质阅读与数字阅读在效果上的差异，部分与纸张的实体特性有关。

paras.en: With paper, there is a literal laying on of hands, along with the visual geography of distinct pages.
paras.zh: 阅读纸质材料时，人们真真切切地用手触碰着书页，而一页页界限分明的纸张还构成了一种视觉布局。

w.m: adj. 真正的；字面意义上的
n. （空间）布局；（各部分的）分布
adj. 分明的；各不相同的

paras.en: People often link their memory of what they’ve read to how far into the book it was or where it was on the page.
paras.zh: 人们常常把对所读内容的记忆，与它在书中的前后位置或在页面上的位置联系起来。

paras.en: But equally important is the mental aspect.
paras.zh: 但同样重要的是心理层面。

paras.en: Reading researchers have proposed a theory called the “shallowing hypothesis (假说)”.
paras.zh: 阅读研究者提出了一种名为“浅层化假说”的理论。

paras.en: According to this theory, people approach digital texts with a mindset suited to social media, which are often not so serious, and devote less mental effort than when they are reading print.
paras.zh: 根据这一理论，人们对待数字文本时，抱着一种适合社交媒体的心态，而社交媒体往往不那么严肃；同时，人们投入的脑力也比阅读纸质读物时少。

paras.en: Audio (音频) and video can feel more engaging than text, and so university teachers increasingly turn to these technologies — say, assigning an online talk instead of an article by the same person.
paras.zh: 音频和视频可能让人觉得比文字更有吸引力，因此大学教师越来越多地转向这些技术——比如，布置某人的在线讲座，而不是此人写的文章。

paras.en: However, psychologists have demonstrated that when adults read news stories, they remember more of the content than if they listen to or view identical pieces.
paras.zh: 然而，心理学家已经证明，成年人阅读新闻报道时记住的内容，比收听或观看内容完全相同的报道时更多。

paras.en: Digital texts, audio and video all have educational roles, especially when providing resources not available in print.
paras.zh: 数字文本、音频和视频都有其教育作用，尤其是在提供纸质版中没有的资源时。

paras.en: However, for maximizing learning where mental focus and reflection are called for, educators shouldn’t assume all media are the same, even when they contain identical words.
paras.zh: 然而，若要在需要专注和反思的情况下最大限度地提高学习效果，教育者不应想当然地认为所有媒介都一样，即便它们包含完全相同的文字。

w.m: v. 想当然地认为；假定

passages.name: 2024 全国新课标Ⅰ卷 阅读D
passages.title: 生物多样性观察数据的偏差
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科学研究
passages.summary: 如今大多数生物多样性记录是照片、视频等数字记录。斯坦福大学达鲁团队利用19亿条记录研究发现，大量仅基于观察的记录并没有带来更好的全球覆盖，而且这些数据偏向某些地区、时间段和物种，包括特征吸引人或引人注目的物种。达鲁认为，生物多样性应用程序可以借助研究结果引导用户去采样不足的地方，并鼓励用户请专家确认上传图片的识别结果，以提高数据质量。

paras.en: In the race to document the species on Earth before they go extinct, researchers and citizen scientists have collected billions of records.
paras.zh: 为了赶在地球上的物种灭绝之前将它们记录下来，研究人员和公民科学家争分夺秒，已经收集了数十亿条记录。

w.m: n. 竞赛；争分夺秒的努力
公民科学家（参与科研的普通公众）

paras.en: Today, most records of biodiversity are in the form of photos, videos, and other digital records.
paras.zh: 如今，大多数生物多样性记录都以照片、视频和其他数字记录的形式存在。

paras.en: Though they are useful for detecting shifts in the number and variety of species in an area, a new Stanford study has found that this type of record is not perfect.
paras.zh: 尽管这些记录有助于发现一个地区内物种数量和种类的变化，但斯坦福大学的一项新研究发现，这类记录并不完美。

paras.en: “With the rise of technology it is easy for people to make observations of different species with the aid of a mobile application,” said Barnabas Daru, who is lead author of the study and assistant professor of biology in the Stanford School of Humanities and Sciences.
paras.zh: “随着技术的兴起，人们借助手机应用程序就能轻松地观察不同的物种，”该研究的第一作者、斯坦福大学人文与科学学院生物学助理教授巴纳巴斯·达鲁说。

paras.en: “These observations now outnumber the primary data that come from physical specimens (标本), and since we are increasingly using observational data to investigate how species are responding to global change, I wanted to know: Are they usable?”
paras.zh: “这些观察记录如今在数量上已超过来自实物标本的原始数据，而且由于我们越来越多地利用观察数据来研究物种如何应对全球变化，我想知道：这些数据能用吗？”

paras.en: Using a global dataset of 1.9 billion records of plants, insects, birds, and other animals, Daru and his team tested how well these data represent actual global biodiversity patterns.
paras.zh: 达鲁和他的团队利用一个包含19亿条植物、昆虫、鸟类和其他动物记录的全球数据集，检验了这些数据能在多大程度上反映真实的全球生物多样性格局。

paras.en: “We were particularly interested in exploring the aspects of sampling that tend to bias (使有偏差) data, like the greater likelihood of a citizen scientist taking a picture of a flowering plant instead of the grass right next to it,” said Daru.
paras.zh: “我们特别感兴趣的是探究采样中容易使数据产生偏差的那些方面，比如公民科学家更有可能拍下一株开花的植物，而不是紧挨着它的草，”达鲁说。

paras.en: Their study revealed that the large number of observation-only records did not lead to better global coverage.
paras.zh: 他们的研究揭示，大量仅基于观察的记录并没有带来更好的全球覆盖。

paras.en: Moreover, these data are biased and favor certain regions, time periods, and species.
paras.zh: 此外，这些数据存在偏差，偏向某些地区、时间段和物种。

w.m: adj. 有偏差的；有偏向的

paras.en: This makes sense because the people who get observational biodiversity data on mobile devices are often citizen scientists recording their encounters with species in areas nearby.
paras.zh: 这不难理解，因为用移动设备获取生物多样性观察数据的人往往是公民科学家，他们记录的是自己在附近地区遇见的物种。

paras.en: These data are also biased toward certain species with attractive or eye-catching features.
paras.zh: 这些数据还偏向于某些特征吸引人或引人注目的物种。

paras.en: What can we do with the imperfect datasets of biodiversity?
paras.zh: 我们能用这些不完美的生物多样性数据集做些什么呢？

w.m: adj. 不完美的；有缺陷的

paras.en: “Quite a lot,” Daru explained.
paras.zh: “能做的有很多，”达鲁解释说。

paras.en: “Biodiversity apps can use our study results to inform users of oversampled areas and lead them to places — and even species — that are not well-sampled.
paras.zh: “生物多样性应用程序可以利用我们的研究结果，告诉用户哪些区域采样过度，并把他们引向采样不足的地方——甚至是采样不足的物种。

paras.en: To improve the quality of observational data, biodiversity apps can also encourage users to have an expert confirm the identification of their uploaded image.”
paras.zh: 为了提高观察数据的质量，生物多样性应用程序还可以鼓励用户请专家确认他们所上传图片的识别结果。”

w.m: 让某人做某事（此处：请专家确认）

passages.name: 2024 全国新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读C
passages.title: 巴比伦微型农场：把菜园搬进室内
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与环保
passages.summary: 商店里的农产品大多要经过长途运输，巴比伦微型农场（BMF）则是一种室内种植系统，可供家庭安装使用，也可服务于医院、餐馆或学校，比农贸市场更能缩短食物从产地到餐桌的路程。它借助云端远程监控和自动化技术，省力省水，运输零排放，也不需要杀虫剂。BMF的员工也在日常生活中践行可持续理念。

paras.en: We all know fresh is best when it comes to food.
paras.zh: 我们都知道，说到食物，新鲜的最好。

paras.en: However, most produce at the store goes through weeks of travel and covers hundreds of miles before reaching the table.
paras.zh: 然而，商店里的大多数农产品在端上餐桌之前，都要经过数周的运输，行程数百英里。

paras.en: While farmers’ markets are a solid choice to reduce the journey, Babylon Micro-Farm (BMF) shortens it even more.
paras.zh: 虽然农贸市场是缩短这段路程的可靠选择，但巴比伦微型农场（BMF）能把这段路程缩得更短。

paras.en: BMF is an indoor garden system.
paras.zh: BMF是一种室内种植系统。

paras.en: It can be set up for a family.
paras.zh: 它可以安装在家里，供一家人使用。

paras.en: Additionally, it could serve a larger audience such as a hospital, restaurant or school.
paras.zh: 此外，它也可以服务于更大的群体，比如医院、餐馆或学校。

paras.en: The innovative design requires little effort to achieve a reliable weekly supply of fresh greens.
paras.zh: 这种创新设计只需花很少的力气，就能实现每周稳定供应新鲜绿叶蔬菜。

paras.en: Specifically, it’s a farm that relies on new technology.
paras.zh: 具体来说，它是一个依靠新技术的农场。

paras.en: Connected through the Cloud, BMF is remotely monitored.
paras.zh: BMF通过云端联网，接受远程监控。

paras.en: Also, there is a convenient app that provides growing data in real time.
paras.zh: 此外，还有一个便捷的应用程序，可以实时提供种植数据。

paras.en: Because the system is automated, it significantly reduces the amount of water needed to grow plants.
paras.zh: 由于该系统是自动化的，因此大大减少了种植植物所需的水量。

paras.en: Rather than watering rows of soil, the system provides just the right amount to each plant.
paras.zh: 该系统不是一垄一垄地给土壤浇水，而是给每株植物提供恰好适量的水。

w.m: n. 一排；一行；（田地的）垄

paras.en: After harvest, users simply replace the plants with a new pre-seeded pod (容器) to get the next growth cycle started.
paras.zh: 收获之后，用户只需用一个新的预播种容器替换掉原来的植物，就能开始下一个生长周期。

paras.en: Moreover, having a system in the same building where the food is eaten means zero emissions (排放) from transporting plants from soil to salad.
paras.zh: 而且，把系统设在人们食用这些食物的同一栋建筑里，意味着植物从土壤到沙拉的运输过程实现零排放。

paras.en: In addition, there’s no need for pesticides and other chemicals that pollute traditional farms and the surrounding environment.
paras.zh: 此外，它也不需要使用会污染传统农场及其周边环境的杀虫剂和其他化学品。

paras.en: BMF employees live out sustainability in their everyday lives.
paras.zh: BMF的员工在日常生活中践行可持续理念。

paras.en: About half of them walk or bike to work.
paras.zh: 其中大约一半人步行或骑自行车上班。

paras.en: Inside the office, they encourage recycling and waste reduction by limiting garbage cans and avoiding single-use plastic.
paras.zh: 在办公室里，他们通过限制垃圾桶数量和避免使用一次性塑料制品，来提倡回收利用、减少废物。

paras.en: “We are passionate about reducing waste, carbon and chemicals in our environment,” said a BMF employee.
paras.zh: “我们热衷于减少环境中的废物、碳和化学物质，”一位BMF员工说。

passages.name: 2024 全国新课标Ⅱ卷 阅读D
passages.title: 书评：应对人工智能未来的实用指南
passages.genre: 书评 · 人工智能与社会
passages.summary: 本文推介卡特里奥娜·坎贝尔的新书《人工智能设计：与人工智能共处的计划》。作者凭借二十多年把高深内容转化为易懂文字的职业经验，从商界人士的实用角度写成了这本通俗易懂、信息丰富的指南。书中指出，人工智能将从当前的“狭义人工智能”发展到通用人工智能，再到主导型人工智能；作者希望唤醒对人工智能负有责任的科技公司和世界各国领导人，并指出我们必须现在就行动、保持对人工智能的控制，通过有条理的思考和随后的全球监管成就伟业，而不是自取灭亡。

paras.en: Given the astonishing potential of AI to transform our lives, we all need to take action to deal with our AI-powered future, and this is where AI by Design: A Plan for Living with Artificial Intelligence comes in.
paras.zh: 鉴于人工智能具有改变我们生活的惊人潜力，我们都需要采取行动，应对由人工智能驱动的未来，而《人工智能设计：与人工智能共处的计划》一书恰好能在这方面派上用场。

w.m: adj. 由人工智能驱动的

paras.en: This absorbing new book by Catriona Campbell is a practical roadmap addressing the challenges posed by the forthcoming AI revolution (变革).
paras.zh: 卡特里奥娜·坎贝尔的这本引人入胜的新书是一份实用的路线图，着眼于应对即将到来的人工智能变革所带来的种种挑战。

paras.en: In the wrong hands, such a book could prove as complicated to process as the computer code (代码) that powers AI, but, thankfully, Campbell has more than two decades’ professional experience translating the heady into the understandable.
paras.zh: 如果由不合适的人来写，这样一本书理解起来可能会和驱动人工智能的计算机代码一样复杂；不过，值得庆幸的是，坎贝尔拥有二十多年把高深内容转化为易懂文字的职业经验。

w.m: 落入不合适的人手中；由不合适的人操刀（此处指由不擅长的作者来写）
adj. 高深的（the heady 指高深难懂的内容）
adj. 易懂的；可以理解的

paras.en: She writes from the practical angle of a business person rather than as an academic, making for a guide which is highly accessible and informative and which, by the close, will make you feel almost as smart as AI.
paras.zh: 她不是以学者的身份，而是从商界人士的实用角度来写作，这使本书成为一本通俗易懂、信息丰富的指南，读到最后，你会觉得自己几乎和人工智能一样聪明。

paras.en: As we soon come to learn from AI by Design, AI is already super-smart and will become more capable, moving from the current generation of “narrow-AI” to Artificial General Intelligence.
paras.zh: 读了《人工智能设计》，我们很快就会了解到，人工智能已经超级聪明，而且还会变得更强大，从当前这一代“狭义人工智能”发展到通用人工智能。

paras.en: From there, Campbell says, will come Artificial Dominant Intelligence.
paras.zh: 坎贝尔说，再往后，就会出现主导型人工智能。

w.m: adj. 主导的；占支配地位的

paras.en: This is why Campbell has set out to raise awareness of AI and its future now — several decades before these developments are expected to take place.
paras.zh: 正因如此，坎贝尔现在就着手提高人们对人工智能及其未来的认识，而这些发展预计要几十年后才会发生。

paras.en: She says it is essential that we keep control of artificial intelligence, or risk being sidelined and perhaps even worse.
paras.zh: 她说，至关重要的是，我们要保持对人工智能的控制，否则就有被边缘化的风险，甚至可能落得更糟的下场。

w.m: v. 使靠边站；使边缘化

paras.en: Campbell’s point is to wake up those responsible for AI — the technology companies and world leaders — so they are on the same page as all the experts currently developing it.
paras.zh: 坎贝尔的用意是唤醒那些对人工智能负有责任的人——科技公司和世界各国领导人——让他们与目前所有正在开发人工智能的专家想法一致。

paras.en: She explains we are at a “tipping point” in history and must act now to prevent an extinction-level event for humanity.
paras.zh: 她解释说，我们正处在历史的“临界点”上，必须现在就行动，防止人类遭遇灭绝级别的事件。

paras.en: We need to consider how we want our future with AI to pan out.
paras.zh: 我们需要思考：我们希望与人工智能共处的未来如何发展。

paras.en: Such structured thinking, followed by global regulation, will enable us to achieve greatness rather than bring about our downfall.
paras.zh: 这样有条理的思考，再加上随后的全球监管，将使我们能够成就伟业，而不是自取灭亡。

w.m: adj. 有条理的；结构化的

paras.en: AI will affect us all, and if you only read one book on the subject, this is it.
paras.zh: 人工智能将影响我们每一个人；如果你只读一本关于这个话题的书，那就读这本吧。

passages.name: 2024 全国甲卷 阅读C
passages.title: 俄罗斯“医疗列车”开进偏远乡村
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 社会与健康
passages.summary: 圣卢卡斯号是俄罗斯政府资助的五列医疗列车之一，开往俄罗斯中部和东部的偏远城镇，为农村居民提供基本医疗、X光检查和开处方等服务。俄罗斯公共医疗服务亟须现代化，这列火车是改善状况的又一尝试。随车拍摄的德国摄影师杜克对医护人员在狭小空间里依然专注、尽心的工作印象深刻。

paras.en: The Saint Lukas train doesn’t accept passengers — it accepts only the sick.
paras.zh: 圣卢卡斯号列车不接载乘客——它只接收病人。

paras.en: The Saint Lukas is one of five government-sponsored medical trains that travel to remote towns in central and eastern Russia.
paras.zh: 圣卢卡斯号是五列由政府资助的医疗列车之一，这些列车开往俄罗斯中部和东部的偏远城镇。

paras.en: Each stop lasts an average of two days, and during that time the doctors and nurses on board provide rural (乡村) populations with basic medical care, X-ray scans and prescriptions.
paras.zh: 每一站平均停留两天，在此期间，车上的医生和护士为农村居民提供基本医疗服务和X光检查，并开具处方。

paras.en: “People started queuing to make an appointment early in the morning,” says Emile Ducke, a German photographer who traveled with the staff of the Saint Lukas on a two-week trip in November through the vast regions (区域) of Krasnoyarsk and Khakassia.
paras.zh: “人们一大早就开始排队预约，”德国摄影师埃米尔·杜克说。11月，他随圣卢卡斯号的工作人员进行了为期两周的旅行，穿越克拉斯诺亚尔斯克和哈卡斯的广袤地区。

w.m: n. 全体员工；工作人员

paras.en: Russia’s public health care service has been in serious need of modernization.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯的公共医疗服务一直迫切需要现代化。

paras.en: The government has struggled to come up with measures to address the problem, particularly in the poorer, rural areas east of the Volga River, including arranging doctor’s appointments by video chat and expanding financial aid programs to motivate doctors to practice medicine in remote parts of the country like Krasnoyarsk.
paras.zh: 政府一直在苦苦思索解决这一问题的办法，尤其是在伏尔加河以东较贫困的农村地区，措施包括安排医生通过视频聊天问诊，以及扩大经济援助项目，激励医生到克拉斯诺亚尔斯克这样的偏远地区行医。

paras.en: The annual arrival of the Saint Lukas is another attempt to improve the situation.
paras.zh: 圣卢卡斯号一年一度的到来，是为改善这一状况所做的又一次尝试。

w.m: adj. 每年一次的；一年一度的

paras.en: For 10 months every year, the train stops at about eight stations over two weeks, before returning to the regional capital to refuel and restock (补给).
paras.zh: 每年有10个月，列车会用两周时间停靠大约8个站点，然后返回地区首府加油、补给。

paras.en: Then it starts all over again the next month.
paras.zh: 到了下个月，它又从头再来。

paras.en: Most stations wait about a year between visits.
paras.zh: 大多数站点要等大约一年才能迎来下一次到访。

paras.en: Doctors see up to 150 patients every day.
paras.zh: 医生们每天要诊治多达150名病人。

paras.en: The train’s equipment allows for basic checkups.
paras.zh: 借助列车上的设备，可以进行基本的身体检查。

paras.en: “I was very impressed by the doctors and their assistants working and living in such little space but still staying focused and very concerned,” says Ducke.
paras.zh: “医生和他们的助手在如此狭小的空间里工作和生活，却依然保持专注、十分尽心，这让我印象深刻，”杜克说。

paras.en: “They were the best chance for many rural people to get the treatment they want.”
paras.zh: “对许多农村居民来说，要得到自己想要的治疗，最好的机会就是他们。”

passages.name: 2024 全国甲卷 阅读D
passages.title: 如何为作品写好结局
passages.genre: 说明文 · 文学与写作
passages.summary: 作者回忆大学时读完《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》后不喜欢其结局，教授引导作者区分“希望人物得到的结局”和“对人物而言恰当的结局”，从此作者对结局有了新的认识，选书也变得更容易。作者指出写结局很难，因为结局在读者心中分量很重；本期《作家文摘》介绍了写好结局的方法，它不会告诉写作者结局该是什么，但可能提供写好结局所需的帮助。

paras.en: “I didn’t like the ending,” I said to my favorite college professor.
paras.zh: “我不喜欢那个结局，”我对大学里最喜欢的那位教授说。

paras.en: It was my junior year of college, and I was doing an independent study on Victorian literature.
paras.zh: 那是我大学三年级的时候，我正在做一项关于维多利亚时代文学的独立研究。

paras.en: I had just finished reading The Mill on the Floss by George Eliot, and I was heartbroken by the ending.
paras.zh: 我刚读完乔治·艾略特的《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》，那个结局让我心碎。

w.m: adj. 心碎的；极度伤心的

paras.en: Prof. Gracie, with all his patience, asked me to think about it beyond whether I liked it or not.
paras.zh: 格雷西教授极有耐心地让我跳出“喜欢不喜欢”的层面，去思考这个结局。

paras.en: He suggested I think about the difference between endings that I wanted for the characters and endings that were right for the characters, endings that satisfied the story even if they didn’t have a traditionally positive outcome.
paras.zh: 他建议我思考两种结局之间的区别：一种是我希望人物得到的结局，另一种是对人物而言恰当的结局，也就是能满足故事需要的结局，哪怕这样的结局在传统意义上并不算好结果。

paras.en: Of course, I would have preferred a different ending for Tom and Maggie Tulliver, but the ending they got did make the most sense for them.
paras.zh: 当然，我本来更希望汤姆和玛吉·塔利弗有一个不同的结局，但他们得到的那个结局对他们来说确实是最合理的。

paras.en: This was an aha moment for me, and I never thought about endings the same way again.
paras.zh: 那一刻我恍然大悟，从此我看待结局的方式再也和从前不一样了。

paras.en: From then on, if I wanted to read an ending guaranteed to be happy, I’d pick up a romance.
paras.zh: 从那以后，如果我想读一个保证圆满的结局，我就会拿起一本爱情小说。

paras.en: If I wanted an ending I couldn’t guess, I’d pick up a mystery (悬疑小说).
paras.zh: 如果想要一个猜不到的结局，我就会拿起一本悬疑小说。

w.m: n. 悬疑小说；侦探小说

paras.en: One where I kind of knew what was going to happen, historical fiction.
paras.zh: 如果想要一个我大致知道会发生什么的结局，就选历史小说。

paras.en: Choosing what to read became easier.
paras.zh: 选择读什么书变得更容易了。

paras.en: But writing the end — that’s hard.
paras.zh: 但写结局——那可就难了。

paras.en: It’s hard for writers because endings carry so much weight with readers.
paras.zh: 这对作家来说很难，因为结局在读者心中分量很重。

w.m: 在……心中有分量；对……有影响力

paras.en: You have to balance creating an ending that’s unpredictable, but doesn’t seem to come from nowhere, one that fits what’s right for the characters.
paras.zh: 你必须把握好平衡，创作出这样一个结局：它出人意料，却又不显得凭空而来，而且符合人物应有的走向。

w.m: adj. 无法预料的；出人意料的

paras.en: That’s why this issue (期) of Writer’s Digest aims to help you figure out how to write the best ending for whatever kind of writing you’re doing.
paras.zh: 正因如此，本期《作家文摘》旨在帮助你弄清楚：无论你在写哪种类型的作品，都该如何写出最好的结局。

w.m: 这就是……的原因；正因如此

paras.en: If it’s short stories, Peter Mountford breaks down six techniques you can try to see which one helps you stick the landing.
paras.zh: 如果你写的是短篇小说，彼得·蒙特福德剖析的六种技巧可供你一试，看看哪一种能帮你稳稳“落地”、漂亮收尾。

paras.en: Elizabeth Sims analyzes the final chapters of five great novels to see what key points they include and how you can adapt them for your work.
paras.zh: 伊丽莎白·西姆斯分析了五部伟大小说的最后几章，看看其中包含了哪些要点，以及你可以如何把这些要点加以调整，运用到自己的作品中。

paras.en: This issue won’t tell you what your ending should be — that’s up to you and the story you’re telling — but it might provide what you need to get there.
paras.zh: 本期不会告诉你结局应该是什么样的——那取决于你和你正在讲述的故事——但它可能会为你提供写出这个结局所需的帮助。

passages.name: 2024 北京卷 阅读C
passages.title: 把宇宙建模为计算机模拟
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科学与哲学
passages.summary: 宇宙是不是一个计算机模拟，并不是一个科学问题，我们很可能永远无法知道答案。作者结合康德的观点和现代科学指出，感知经验和推理都无法揭示现实，宇宙是不可知的，因此不妨把问题转为“能否把宇宙建模为计算机模拟”。模型并不是现实，而是应对未知、做出发现的工具；作者认为，构建这一新模型也将是一项回报极大的工作。

paras.en: The notion that we live in someone else’s video game is irresistible to many.
paras.zh: 认为我们生活在别人的电子游戏里，这种想法对许多人来说有着难以抗拒的吸引力。

w.m: adj. 极具吸引力的；无法抗拒的

paras.en: Searching the term “simulation hypothesis” (模拟假说) returns numerous results that debate whether the universe is a computer simulation — a concept that some scientists actually take seriously.
paras.zh: 搜索“模拟假说”这个词，会得到大量搜索结果，都在争论宇宙是不是计算机模拟——一些科学家确实认真对待这个概念。

paras.en: Unfortunately, this is not a scientific question.
paras.zh: 遗憾的是，这不是一个科学问题。

w.m: adv. 遗憾的是；不幸的是

paras.en: We will probably never know whether it’s true.
paras.zh: 我们很可能永远无从知道这一说法是否属实。

paras.en: We can, instead, use this idea to advance scientific knowledge.
paras.zh: 不过，我们可以转而利用这个想法来推动科学知识的发展。

paras.en: The 18th-century philosopher Kant argued that the universe ultimately consists of things-in-themselves that are unknowable.
paras.zh: 18世纪的哲学家康德认为，宇宙归根结底是由不可知的“物自体”构成的。

w.m: n. 物自体（康德哲学术语）

paras.en: While he held the notion that objective reality exists, he said our mind plays a necessary role in structuring and shaping our perceptions.
paras.zh: 虽然他持有“客观现实是存在的”这一观点，但他也说，我们的心智在构建和塑造感知的过程中起着必不可少的作用。

paras.en: Modern sciences have revealed that our perceptual experience of the world is the result of many stages of processing by sensory systems and cognitive (认知的) functions in the brain.
paras.zh: 现代科学已经揭示，我们对世界的感知体验，是大脑中的感觉系统和认知功能经过许多阶段处理的结果。

paras.en: No one knows exactly what happens within this black box.
paras.zh: 没有人确切知道这个黑箱里发生了什么。

w.m: 黑箱（内部情况不明的系统）

paras.en: If empirical (实证的) experience fails to reveal reality, reasoning won’t reveal reality either since it relies on concepts and words that are contingent on our social, cultural and psychological histories.
paras.zh: 如果实证经验无法揭示现实，那么推理也同样无法揭示现实，因为推理所依赖的概念和词语，取决于我们在社会、文化和心理方面的经历。

w.m: adj. 实证的；以经验为依据的

paras.en: Again, a black box.
paras.zh: 又是一个黑箱。

w.m: 黑箱（内部情况不明的系统）

paras.en: So, if we accept that the universe is unknowable, we also accept we will never know if we live in a computer simulation.
paras.zh: 所以，如果我们接受宇宙不可知，也就接受了：我们永远不会知道自己是否生活在计算机模拟之中。

paras.en: And then, we can shift our inquiry from “Is the universe a computer simulation?” to “Can we model the universe as a computer simulation?”
paras.zh: 这样一来，我们就可以把探究的问题从“宇宙是计算机模拟吗？”转向“我们能否把宇宙建模为计算机模拟？”

paras.en: Modelling reality is what we do.
paras.zh: 为现实建模，本来就是我们一直在做的事。

w.m: v. 为……建模；构建……的模型

paras.en: To facilitate our comprehension of the world, we build models based on conceptual metaphors (隐喻) that are familiar to us.
paras.zh: 为了便于理解世界，我们以自己熟悉的概念隐喻为基础来构建模型。

paras.en: In Newton’s era, we imagined the universe as a clock.
paras.zh: 在牛顿的时代，我们把宇宙想象成一座时钟。

paras.en: In Einstein’s, we uncovered the standard model of particle (粒子) physics.
paras.zh: 在爱因斯坦的时代，我们发现了粒子物理学的标准模型。

w.m: 标准模型（粒子物理学理论）

paras.en: Now that we are in the information age, we have new concepts such as the computer, information processing, virtual reality, and simulation.
paras.zh: 由于如今身处信息时代，我们有了诸如计算机、信息处理、虚拟现实和模拟这样的新概念。

paras.en: Unsurprisingly, these new concepts inspire us to build new models of the universe.
paras.zh: 不出所料，这些新概念启发我们构建新的宇宙模型。

paras.en: Models are not the reality, however.
paras.zh: 然而，模型并不是现实。

paras.en: There is no point in arguing whether the universe is a clock, a set of particles or an output of computation.
paras.zh: 争论宇宙是一座时钟、一组粒子还是计算的产物，是没有意义的。

paras.en: All these models are tools to deal with the unknown and to make discoveries.
paras.zh: 所有这些模型都是用来应对未知、有所发现的工具。

paras.en: And the more tools we have, the more effective and insightful we can become.
paras.zh: 而且，我们拥有的工具越多，就能变得越高效、越有洞察力。

w.m: adj. 有洞察力的；富有见地的

paras.en: It can be imagined that, comparable to the process of building previous scientific models, developing the “computer simulation” metaphor-based model will also be a hugely rewarding exercise.
paras.zh: 可以想象，与以往构建科学模型的过程相似，开发基于“计算机模拟”这一隐喻的模型也将是一项回报极大的工作。

w.m: adj. 有回报的；值得做的
n. （有特定目的的）活动；工作

passages.name: 2024 北京卷 阅读D
passages.title: 人类道德规范从何而来
passages.genre: 说明文 · 人类与道德
passages.summary: 文章以19世纪因纽特人的生活为例，说明早期人类可能遵循的道德准则。作者指出，不同文化的道德美德惊人地相似，这些普遍规范远早于宣扬道德的宗教和成文法的出现，根植于人类相似的基本需求和共有的学习机制。社会本能和一个被改作他用的奖励系统帮助我们养成良好的社会习惯、形成是非观；增大的大脑增强了自控能力和解决问题的能力，语言能力又进一步强化了这些能力。

paras.en: Franz Boas’s description of Inuit (因纽特人) life in the 19th century illustrates the probable moral code of early humans.
paras.zh: 弗朗茨·博厄斯对19世纪因纽特人生活的描述，说明了早期人类很可能遵循的道德准则。

paras.en: Here, norms (规范) were unwritten and rarely expressed clearly, but were well understood and taken to heart.
paras.zh: 在因纽特人的社会里，规范是不成文的，也很少被明确地表达出来，但人们都很清楚这些规范，并将其铭记于心。

paras.en: Dishonest and violent behaviours were disapproved of; leadership, marriage and interactions with other groups were loosely governed by traditions.
paras.zh: 不诚实和暴力的行为不被认可；领导方式、婚姻以及与其他群体的交往，都由传统加以约束，但约束并不严格。

w.m: n. 领导（方式）；领导地位

paras.en: Conflict was often resolved in musical battles.
paras.zh: 冲突常常在音乐对决中得到化解。

paras.en: Because arguing angrily leads to chaos, it was strongly discouraged.
paras.zh: 由于怒气冲冲地争吵会导致混乱，这种做法受到强烈反对。

paras.en: With life in unforgiving northern Canada being so demanding, the Inuit’s practical approach to morality made good sense.
paras.zh: 在严酷的加拿大北部，生活如此艰难，因纽特人以务实的态度对待道德，也就很有道理了。

paras.en: The similarity of moral virtues across cultures is striking, even though the relative ranking of the virtues may vary with a social group’s history and environment.
paras.zh: 不同文化中的道德美德惊人地相似，尽管这些美德的相对排序可能因社会群体的历史和环境而有所不同。

paras.en: Typically, cruelty and cheating are discouraged, while cooperation, humbleness and courage are praised.
paras.zh: 通常，残忍和欺骗会遭到反对，而合作、谦逊和勇气则受到赞扬。

paras.en: These universal norms far pre-date the concept of any moralising religion or written law.
paras.zh: 这些普遍的规范远在任何宣扬道德的宗教或成文法的概念出现之前就已存在。

w.m: adj. 宣扬道德的；进行道德教化的

paras.en: Instead, they are rooted in the similarity of basic human needs and our shared mechanisms for learning and problem solving.
paras.zh: 它们其实根植于人类基本需求的相似性，以及我们共有的学习和解决问题的机制。

paras.en: Our social instincts (本能) include the intense desire to belong.
paras.zh: 我们的社会本能包括对归属感的强烈渴望。

paras.en: The approval of others is rewarding, while their disapproval is strongly disliked.
paras.zh: 得到他人的认可令人满足，而遭到他人的否定则让人非常反感。

w.m: adj. 令人满足的；有回报的

paras.en: These social emotions prepare our brains to shape our behaviour according to the norms and values of our family and our community.
paras.zh: 这些社会情感使我们的大脑做好准备，依照家庭和群体的规范与价值观来塑造我们的行为。

paras.en: More generally, social instincts motivate us to learn how to behave in a socially complex world.
paras.zh: 更广泛地说，社会本能促使我们去学习如何在社会关系复杂的世界里为人处世。

paras.en: The mechanism involves a repurposed reward system originally used to develop habits important for self-care.
paras.zh: 这一机制涉及一个被改作他用的奖励系统，它最初用于养成对自我照料很重要的习惯。

paras.en: Our brains use the system to acquire behavioural patterns regarding safe routes home, efficient food gathering and dangers to avoid.
paras.zh: 我们的大脑利用这一系统，习得关于安全的回家路线、高效采集食物以及需要避开的危险等方面的行为模式。

paras.en: Good habits save time, energy and sometimes your life.
paras.zh: 好习惯能节省时间和精力，有时还能救你一命。

paras.en: Good social habits do something similar in a social context.
paras.zh: 良好的社会习惯在社会环境中也起着类似的作用。

paras.en: We learn to tell the truth, even when lying is self-serving; we help a grandparent even when it is inconvenient.
paras.zh: 我们学会说真话，即使撒谎对自己有利；我们帮助祖父母，即使这样做并不方便。

w.m: adj. 利己的；为自己谋利的

paras.en: We acquire what we call a sense of right and wrong.
paras.zh: 我们习得了所谓的是非观。

w.h: a sense of right and wrong

paras.en: Social benefits are accompanied by social demands: we must get along, but not put up with too much.
paras.zh: 社会层面的好处伴随着社会层面的要求：我们必须与人和睦相处，但也不能一味忍让。

paras.en: Hence self-discipline is advantageous.
paras.zh: 因此，自律是有益的。

paras.en: In humans, a greatly enlarged brain boosts self-control, just as it boosts problem-solving skills in the social as well as the physical world.
paras.zh: 人类的大脑大幅增大，增强了自控能力，正如它也增强了人们在社会世界以及物质世界中解决问题的能力一样。

paras.en: These abilities are strengthened by our capacity for language, which allows social practices to develop in extremely unobvious ways.
paras.zh: 这些能力因我们的语言能力而得到强化，语言能力使社会习俗能够以极难察觉的方式发展。

w.m: adj. 不明显的；不易察觉的

passages.name: 2024 天津卷（第一次·3月） 阅读C
passages.title: “卷毛狗”老师的一堂课
passages.genre: 记叙文 · 人物与成长
passages.summary: 作者艾迪朗读出色，谢瓦利埃小姐请她在周六晚间俱乐部背诵朗费罗的一首诗。排练时，她不清楚“impetuous”一词的读音和意思，老师假装没注意到她的窘迫，递给她一本词典，让她读出释义并说出自己的看法，还告诉她女孩子也应足够明智，在需要时接受挑战。从那以后，作者再也不叫老师“卷毛狗”了。

paras.en: Our teacher, Miss Chevalier, was a small woman, with a moon face, plump fingers and curls that sprang straight up from her head, hence the funny name “Poodle (卷毛狗)”.
paras.zh: 我们的老师谢瓦利埃小姐是个身材娇小的女人，圆圆的脸，手指胖乎乎的，一头卷发直直地竖在头上，因此有了“卷毛狗”这个滑稽的外号。

paras.en: She taught in our reading club.
paras.zh: 她在我们的读书俱乐部教课。

paras.en: Sometimes she would look in and ask what we were reading — not to check but to know.
paras.zh: 有时她会进来看看，问我们在读什么——不是为了检查，而是想了解。

paras.en: That’s what happened the day my club was reading aloud a poem by Henry Longfellow.
paras.zh: 我们俱乐部朗读亨利·朗费罗的一首诗那天，就发生了这样的事。

paras.en: I guess I was better than the others, for Miss Chevalier asked a while later, “Addie, I was wondering if you would recite the whole poem to the Saturday evening club.”
paras.zh: 我想我读得比其他人好，因为过了一会儿，谢瓦利埃小姐问道：“艾迪，我在想，你愿不愿意在周六晚间俱乐部活动上背诵整首诗。”

paras.en: She said a famous professor was going to give a lecture about the poet, and a presentation of that poem would be a fresh way to start.
paras.zh: 她说，一位著名教授要来做一场关于这位诗人的讲座，而以朗诵那首诗来开场会很新颖。

paras.en: She asked me to memorize it.
paras.zh: 她让我把这首诗背下来。

paras.en: “But that shouldn’t be a problem for a child of your ability,” she added.
paras.zh: “不过对于像你这样有能力的孩子来说，这应该不成问题，”她补充道。

paras.en: I’m telling you, my happy feet barely touched the ground all the way home.
paras.zh: 说真的，回家的一路上，我高兴得脚都快不沾地了。

paras.en: To me, that was the biggest thing ever and I soon learned the whole poem by heart, well prepared for our first rehearsal.
paras.zh: 对我来说，那是我经历过的最了不起的事。我很快就把整首诗背得滚瓜烂熟，为第一次排练做好了充分准备。

paras.en: I was desperately nervous when I went to her office the next day.
paras.zh: 第二天去她办公室时，我紧张得要命。

paras.en: But the good thing was she always had the smile that would make you feel like you just did something right.
paras.zh: 不过好在她总是带着那种微笑，让你觉得自己好像刚做对了什么事。

paras.en: Halfway through the poem, Miss Chevalier stopped me and asked if I knew what “impetuous” meant.
paras.zh: 诗背到一半时，谢瓦利埃小姐打断了我，问我知不知道“impetuous”是什么意思。

paras.en: Despite her encouraging smile, I wanted to sink through the floor because I was unsure about its pronunciation as well as its meaning.
paras.zh: 尽管她带着鼓励的微笑，我还是恨不得找个地缝钻进去，因为这个词的读音和意思我都没有把握。

paras.en: Miss Chevalier pretended not to have noticed my red face and handed me a dictionary, asking me to read the word’s definition aloud.
paras.zh: 谢瓦利埃小姐假装没注意到我涨红的脸，递给我一本词典，让我把这个词的释义大声读出来。

paras.en: “Impetuous has two definitions: rushing with great force or violence; acting suddenly, with little thought.”
paras.zh: “impetuous有两个释义：一是以巨大的力量或猛烈之势向前冲；二是行事突然，几乎不加思考。”

paras.en: She asked me which one fitted the poem.
paras.zh: 她问我哪一个释义符合诗中的意思。

paras.en: I read both definitions over again, trying to figure it out, but Miss Chevalier must have read my mind.
paras.zh: 我把两个释义又读了一遍，想弄明白，但谢瓦利埃小姐一定是看出了我的心思。

paras.en: “There is no wrong answer,” she said.
paras.zh: “怎么回答都不算错，”她说。

paras.en: “I want to know your opinion, Addie.”
paras.zh: “我想知道你的看法，艾迪。”

paras.en: Hesitantly, I said, “Maybe… both.”
paras.zh: 我犹豫地说：“也许……两个都是。”

paras.en: She liked that.
paras.zh: 她喜欢这个回答。

paras.en: “One has to be impetuous both ways or one wouldn’t dare to face up to any challenge.
paras.zh: “一个人得在两种意义上都‘冲动’才行，否则就不敢直面任何挑战。

paras.en: Would you call yourself impetuous?”
paras.zh: 你会说自己是个冲动的人吗？”

w.m: adj. 冲动的；（做事）有冲劲的

paras.en: I knew she was asking for an opinion.
paras.zh: 我知道她是在征求我的看法。

paras.en: “My mother thinks it is improper for girls to be impetuous, anyway.”
paras.zh: “反正我妈妈认为女孩子冲动是不得体的。”

w.m: adj. 不得体的；不恰当的

paras.en: She said my mom was somewhat right about that.
paras.zh: 她说我妈妈在这一点上有几分道理。

paras.en: “But girls should also be wise enough to take up challenges when needed.
paras.zh: “但女孩子也应该足够明智，在需要时接受挑战。

paras.en: I believe you are such a girl.”
paras.zh: 我相信你就是这样的女孩。”

paras.en: After that, I would never call Miss Chevalier “Poodle” again.
paras.zh: 从那以后，我再也不叫谢瓦利埃小姐“卷毛狗”了。

passages.name: 2024 天津卷（第一次·3月） 阅读D
passages.title: 北极湖泊为何提前消失
passages.genre: 说明文 · 自然与环境
passages.summary: 人们原以为气候变暖会使北极湖泊扩大，但科学家观察到，一些湖泊在短时间内急剧缩小甚至完全消失，比预测早了一个世纪。永冻层融化后，更多的水能够渗入地下；新证据表明，降雨（尤其是日益增多的秋雨）正大大加剧永冻层的消失，而现有的气候模型都没有包含这一过程。作者由此指出，我们需要对自然界进行直接观测。

paras.en: Research sometimes proves, with data, what we more or less already know (e.g. exercise is good for you, and polluted air isn’t).
paras.zh: 研究有时会用数据证明我们多少已经知道的事情（例如，锻炼对身体有益，而污染的空气则对身体无益）。

paras.en: Still, sometimes our assumptions are incorrect, and scientific findings surprise researchers, along with the rest of us.
paras.zh: 不过，有时我们的假设并不正确，科学发现会让研究人员以及我们其他人都感到意外。

paras.en: A recent example is the phenomenon of disappearing lakes in parts of the frozen treeless Arctic (北极的) region.
paras.zh: 最近的一个例子是，在冰冻、无树的北极地区，部分区域出现了湖泊消失的现象。

paras.en: You might think these lakes would be expanding, not disappearing.
paras.zh: 你可能会以为这些湖泊会不断扩大，而不是消失。

paras.en: As climate change warms the region — melting (融化) surface snow and ice as well as the permafrost (永冻层) — there should be more surface water, forming larger lakes and even new ones.
paras.zh: 随着气候变化使该地区变暖——融化地表的冰雪以及永冻层——地表水应该会增多，形成更大的湖泊，甚至形成新的湖泊。

paras.en: Recently, however, scientists have observed not just shrinking (缩小的) lakes but lakes that have completely gone away.
paras.zh: 然而，最近科学家们观察到的不仅有正在缩小的湖泊，还有已经完全消失的湖泊。

paras.en: Many scientists shared the commonsense expectation that as permafrost melted, lakes would at first expand with meltwater flowing into them.
paras.zh: 许多科学家都持有一种常识性的预期：随着永冻层融化，湖泊起初会因融水流入而扩大。

w.m: v. 共有，共同持有（看法、预期等）

paras.en: Researchers also predicted that eventually progressive warming during the 21st and 22nd centuries would dry out the Arctic, and lakes would begin to shrink.
paras.zh: 研究人员还预测，21世纪和22世纪逐渐加剧的变暖最终会使北极变得干燥，湖泊也会开始缩小。

w.m: adj. 逐渐加剧的；逐步发展的

paras.en: But now it looks as if Arctic lakes are disappearing a century sooner than predicted.
paras.zh: 但现在看来，北极湖泊消失的时间比预测的早了一个世纪。

w.m: adv. 早；快（比较级 sooner：更早）

paras.en: A case in point is that some large, age-old lakes shrank dramatically in what appears to have been a matter of months.
paras.zh: 一个典型的例子是，一些古老的大型湖泊在似乎只有短短几个月的时间里急剧缩小。

w.m: adj. 古老的；由来已久的

paras.en: Scientists have labeled this phenomenon “disastrous lake loss”.
paras.zh: 科学家们将这一现象称为“灾难性湖泊消失”。

paras.en: What caused this?
paras.zh: 是什么导致了这种情况？

paras.en: The frozen solid ground actually contains bits of rock, mineral and organic matter, leaving spaces in between.
paras.zh: 冻得坚硬的地面实际上含有岩石、矿物和有机物的碎块，碎块之间留有空隙。

paras.en: Because these spaces are filled with solid ice, liquid water cannot readily get inside; when the permafrost melts, however, more water can get through.
paras.zh: 由于这些空隙里填满了固态冰，液态水不易渗入；然而，永冻层融化时，更多的水就能渗透进去。

paras.en: In one case, soon after the permafrost beneath them melted, around 192 lakes in northwestern Alaska disappeared from sight.
paras.zh: 有一个例子是，阿拉斯加西北部约192个湖泊在湖底的永冻层融化后不久就消失不见了。

w.m: 从视野中消失；消失不见

paras.en: Why did scientists miss this?
paras.zh: 科学家们为什么没能预见到这一点？

paras.en: One probable reason is that most climate models assume that the melting of permafrost is driven only by warming air.
paras.zh: 一个可能的原因是，大多数气候模型都假定，永冻层融化仅仅是空气变暖造成的。

paras.en: New evidence suggests, however, that rainfall — particularly increasing autumn rain — is now contributing significantly to permafrost loss.
paras.zh: 然而，新的证据表明，降雨——尤其是日益增多的秋雨——目前正在大大加剧永冻层的消失。

paras.en: The rainfall carries heat into the ground.
paras.zh: 雨水将热量带入地下。

paras.en: Yet none of the existing models includes such processes.
paras.zh: 然而，现有的模型都没有把这样的过程考虑在内。

paras.en: That is a good example of why — no matter how complex our models are or may one day be — we need direct observation of the natural world.
paras.zh: 这很好地说明了为什么无论我们的模型现在有多复杂，或者将来有一天可能变得多复杂，我们都需要对自然界进行直接观测。

passages.name: 2024 浙江卷（1月） 阅读C
passages.title: 人工播云防雹引发的争议
passages.genre: 说明文 · 科技与社会
passages.summary: 1991年卡尔加里遭受加拿大历史上损失最惨重的雹暴后，自1996年起，一批保险公司每年花费约200万美元资助艾伯塔省的防雹项目，用飞机播云让小冰晶以降雨形式落下。下风处的农民担心播云夺走土地的水分、增加干旱风险，项目负责人则认为，播云只影响空气中水分总量的极小一部分，不可能导致干旱。也有科学家怀疑播云的安全性；但由于缺乏关于其影响的科学证据，至今无人打赢针对播云公司的诉讼，私人气候工程得以在法律上相对安全地进行。

paras.en: On September 7, 1991, the costliest hailstorm (雹暴) in Canadian history hit Calgary’s southern suburbs.
paras.zh: 1991年9月7日，加拿大历史上损失最惨重的一场雹暴袭击了卡尔加里南部的郊区。

w.m: adj. 代价高昂的；损失惨重的

paras.en: As a result, since 1996 a group of insurance companies have spent about $2 million per year on the Alberta Hail Suppression Project.
paras.zh: 因此，自1996年以来，一批保险公司每年在“艾伯塔防雹项目”上花费约200万美元。

paras.en: Airplanes seed threatening storm cells with a chemical to make small ice crystals fall as rain before they can grow into dangerous hailstones.
paras.zh: 飞机向有威胁的风暴单体播撒一种化学物质，使小冰晶在长成危险的冰雹之前就以雨的形式落下。

w.m: v. （向云中）播撒（催化剂）；播种

paras.en: But farmers in east-central Alberta — downwind of the hail project flights — worry that precious moisture (水分) is being stolen from their thirsty land by the cloud seeding.
paras.zh: 但是，艾伯塔省中东部的农民——他们正处在防雹项目飞行航线的下风处——担心播云正在偷走他们干渴土地上的宝贵水分。

paras.en: Norman Stienwand, who farms in that area, has been addressing public meetings on this issue for years.
paras.zh: 诺曼·斯廷万德在那个地区务农，多年来一直就这个问题在公众集会上发表讲话。

paras.en: “Basically, the provincial government is letting the insurance companies protect the Calgary-Edmonton urban area from hail,” Mr. Stienwand says, “but they’re increasing drought risk as far east as Saskatchewan.”
paras.zh: “说白了，省政府是在让保险公司保护卡尔加里—埃德蒙顿城区免遭冰雹袭击，”斯廷万德先生说，“但他们却在加大干旱风险，波及范围向东远至萨斯喀彻温省。”

paras.en: The Alberta hail project is managed by Terry Krauss, a cloud physicist who works for Weather Modification Inc. of Fargo, North Dakota.
paras.zh: 艾伯塔防雹项目由特里·克劳斯管理，他是一位云物理学家，就职于北达科他州法戈市的天气调控公司。

paras.en: “We affect only a very small percentage of the total moisture in the air, so we cannot be causing drought,” Dr. Krauss says.
paras.zh: “我们影响的只是空气中水分总量的极小一部分，所以我们不可能导致干旱，”克劳斯博士说。

paras.en: “In fact, we may be helping increase the moisture downwind by creating wetter ground.”
paras.zh: “事实上，我们让地面变得更湿润，这可能正有助于增加下风处的水分。”

paras.en: One doubter about the safety of cloud seeding is Chuck Doswell, a research scientist who just retired from the University of Oklahoma.
paras.zh: 对播云安全性持怀疑态度的人当中，有一位是查克·多斯韦尔，他是一名刚从俄克拉何马大学退休的研究科学家。

paras.en: “In 1999, I personally saw significant tornadoes (龙卷风) form from a seeded storm cell in Kansas,” Dr. Doswell says.
paras.zh: “1999年，我亲眼看到堪萨斯州一个播撒过催化剂的风暴单体中形成了强龙卷风，”多斯韦尔博士说。

paras.en: “Does cloud seeding create killer storms or reduce moisture downwind?
paras.zh: “播云会不会引发致命的风暴，或者减少下风处的水分？

paras.en: No one really knows, of course, but the seeding goes on.”
paras.zh: 当然，谁也说不清，但播云仍在继续。”

paras.en: Given the degree of doubt, Mr. Stienwand suggests, “it would be wise to stop cloud seeding.”
paras.zh: 鉴于疑虑如此之大，斯廷万德先生建议：“停止播云会是明智之举。”

paras.en: In practice, doubt has had the opposite effect.
paras.zh: 实际上，疑虑却产生了相反的效果。

paras.en: Due to the lack of scientific proof concerning their impacts, no one has succeeded in winning a lawsuit against cloud-seeding companies.
paras.zh: 由于缺乏有关播云影响的科学证据，至今没有人成功打赢针对播云公司的诉讼。

paras.en: Hence, private climate engineering can proceed in relative legal safety.
paras.zh: 因此，私人气候工程可以在法律上相对安全地进行。

passages.name: 2024 浙江卷（1月） 阅读D
passages.title: 抵制信息时代的“棉花糖”
passages.genre: 议论文 · 科技与生活
passages.summary: 斯坦福棉花糖实验发现，孩子能否为得到第二块甜食而等待，与日后多种形式的成功有关。作者认为，成年人每天面对的电子设备和信息就像孩子面前的棉花糖：我们的大脑在热量和信息都匮乏的环境中形成，至今未变，因此难以抗拒诱惑。作者主张像审慎对待热量摄入一样审慎对待信息摄入，抵制精神“垃圾食品”，以最有效地管理时间。

paras.en: The Stanford marshmallow (棉花糖) test was originally conducted by psychologist Walter Mischel in the late 1960s.
paras.zh: 斯坦福棉花糖实验最初是由心理学家沃尔特·米舍尔在20世纪60年代末进行的。

paras.en: Children aged four to six at a nursery school were placed in a room.
paras.zh: 一所幼儿园里四到六岁的孩子被安排在一个房间里。

paras.en: A single sugary treat, selected by the child, was placed on a table.
paras.zh: 桌子上放了一块由孩子自己挑选的甜食。

w.m: n. 难得的美食；（特别的）享受

paras.en: Each child was told that if they waited for 15 minutes before eating the treat, they would be given a second treat.
paras.zh: 每个孩子都被告知：如果等15分钟再吃这块甜食，就会得到第二块甜食。

w.m: adj. 第二个的；又一个的

paras.en: Then they were left alone in the room.
paras.zh: 然后，他们被单独留在房间里。

paras.en: Follow-up studies with the children later in life showed a connection between an ability to wait long enough to obtain a second treat and various forms of success.
paras.zh: 日后对这些孩子进行的跟踪研究表明，为获得第二块甜食而等待足够长时间的能力，与各种形式的成功之间存在关联。

paras.en: As adults we face a version of the marshmallow test every day.
paras.zh: 作为成年人，我们每天都要面对某种形式的棉花糖实验。

w.m: n. 版本；（某事物的）一种形式

paras.en: We’re tempted (诱惑) not by sugary treats but by our computers, phones, and tablets — all the devices that connect us to the global delivery system for various types of information that do to us what marshmallows do to preschoolers.
paras.zh: 诱惑我们的不是甜食，而是我们的电脑、手机和平板电脑——所有这些设备把我们与传送各类信息的全球系统连接起来，而这些信息对我们的作用，就如同棉花糖对学龄前儿童的作用。

paras.en: We are tempted by sugary treats because our ancestors lived in a calorie-poor world, and our brains developed a response mechanism to these treats that reflected their value — a feeling of reward and satisfaction.
paras.zh: 我们之所以受甜食诱惑，是因为我们的祖先生活在一个热量匮乏的世界里，而我们的大脑对这类食物形成了一种能体现其价值的反应机制——一种奖赏感和满足感。

paras.en: But as we’ve reshaped the world around us, dramatically reducing the cost and effort involved in obtaining calories, we still have the same brains we had thousands of years ago, and this mismatch is at the heart of why so many of us struggle to resist tempting foods that we know we shouldn’t eat.
paras.zh: 然而，尽管我们已经重塑了周围的世界，大大减少了获取热量所需的成本和精力，我们的大脑却仍和几千年前一样；这种不匹配，正是我们当中这么多人明知有些诱人的食物不该吃、却难以抗拒的根本原因。

paras.en: A similar process is at work in our response to information.
paras.zh: 我们对信息的反应中也有类似的过程在起作用。

paras.en: Our formative environment as a species was information-poor, so our brains developed a mechanism that prized new information.
paras.zh: 作为一个物种，我们在形成时期所处的环境信息匮乏，因此大脑发展出了一种重视新信息的机制。

w.m: adj. 形成期的；对形成有重大影响的

paras.en: But global connectivity has greatly changed our information environment.
paras.zh: 然而，全球互联已经极大地改变了我们的信息环境。

paras.en: We are now ceaselessly bombarded (轰炸) with new information.
paras.zh: 如今，我们不断受到新信息的狂轰滥炸。

w.m: v. 轰炸；（用大量信息等）不断冲击

paras.en: Therefore, just as we need to be more thoughtful about our caloric consumption, we also need to be more thoughtful about our information consumption, resisting the temptation of the mental “junk food” in order to manage our time most effectively.
paras.zh: 因此，正如我们需要更加审慎地对待热量摄入一样，我们也需要更加审慎地对待信息摄入，抵制精神“垃圾食品”的诱惑，以便最有效地管理我们的时间。

passages.name: 2025 全国一卷 阅读C
passages.title: 把街道还给行人
passages.genre: 说明文 · 书评与城市生活
passages.summary: 近年来街道的安全性或许有所改善，但行人（尤其是儿童）的出行能力却在下降，许多家长因路上车太多、孩子步行不安全而改为开车送孩子上学。两位荷兰作者在新书《出行》中呼吁重新思考街道的作用。几十年前，城市就开始围绕汽车重新规划，简·雅各布斯等人曾发起抗争；如今澳大利亚的汽车拥有率位居世界前列。本文作者赞同《出行》两位作者的观点：是时候换个角度看待家门口的街道了。

paras.en: While safety improvements might have been made to our streets in recent years, transport studies also show declines in pedestrian (行人) mobility, especially among young children.
paras.zh: 虽然近年来我们的街道在安全方面可能有所改善，但交通研究也显示，行人的出行能力在下降，在年幼的孩子中尤为明显。

w.m: n. 移动能力；出行能力

paras.en: Many parents say there’s too much traffic on the roads for their children to walk safely to school, so they pack them into the car instead.
paras.zh: 许多家长说，路上车太多，孩子没法安全地步行上学，所以他们改为把孩子塞进车里，开车送去上学。

paras.en: Dutch authors Thalia Verkade and Marco te Brömmelstroet are bothered by facts like these.
paras.zh: 荷兰作者塔利娅·费尔卡德和马尔科·特·布罗梅尔斯特鲁特对这样的事实感到困扰。

paras.en: In their new book Movement: How to Take Back Our Streets and Transform Our Lives, they call for a rethink of our streets and the role they play in our lives.
paras.zh: 在他们的新书《出行：如何夺回我们的街道，改变我们的生活》中，他们呼吁重新思考我们的街道，以及街道在我们生活中所扮演的角色。

paras.en: Life on city streets started to change decades ago.
paras.zh: 城市街道上的生活早在几十年前就开始改变了。

paras.en: Whole neighbourhoods were destroyed to make way for new road networks and kids had to play elsewhere.
paras.zh: 整片整片的街区被拆毁，为新的道路网络让路，孩子们只好到别处去玩。

paras.en: Some communities fought back.
paras.zh: 一些社区奋起反抗。

paras.en: Most famously, an American-Canadian journalist who lived in Manhattan in the 1950s led a campaign to stop the destruction of her local park.
paras.zh: 最有名的是，一位20世纪50年代住在曼哈顿的美国裔加拿大记者领导了一场运动，阻止当地公园被毁。

paras.en: Describing her alarm at its proposed replacement with an expressway, Jane Jacobs called on her mayor (市长) to champion “New York as a decent place to live, and not just rush through.”
paras.zh: 简·雅各布斯表达了她对有人提议用高速公路取代这座公园的担忧，呼吁市长捍卫“纽约作为一个宜居之地，而不只是一个匆匆通过的地方”的地位。

w.m: adj. 像样的；令人满意的

paras.en: Similar campaigns occurred in Australia in the late 1960s and 1970s as well.
paras.zh: 20世纪60年代末和70年代，澳大利亚也发生过类似的运动。

paras.en: Although these campaigns were widespread, the reality is that the majority of western cities were completely redesigned around the needs of the motor car.
paras.zh: 尽管这些运动很普遍，但现实是，大多数西方城市都完全围绕汽车的需要重新设计了。

paras.en: The number of cars on roads has been increasing rapidly.
paras.zh: 路上的汽车数量一直在迅速增加。

paras.en: In Australia we now have over twenty million cars for just over twenty-six million people, among the highest rates of car ownership in the world.
paras.zh: 在澳大利亚，如今我们2600万出头的人口拥有2000多万辆汽车，汽车拥有率位居世界前列。

paras.en: We invest a lot in roads that help us rush through, but we fail to account for the true costs.
paras.zh: 我们在能让我们匆匆通过的道路上投入很多，却没有把真正的代价考虑在内。

paras.en: Do we really recognise what it costs us as a society when children can’t move safely around our communities?
paras.zh: 当孩子们无法在社区里安全走动时，我们真的意识到这让整个社会付出了什么代价吗？

paras.en: The authors of Movement have it right: it’s time to think differently about that street outside your front door.
paras.zh: 《出行》的作者说得对：是时候换个角度看待你家门外的那条街了。

passages.name: 2025 全国一卷 阅读D
passages.title: 把自来水煮沸再过滤，可去除大部分微塑料
passages.genre: 说明文 · 健康与环境
passages.summary: 微塑料已遍布地球，甚至出现在人体内。中国研究人员发现，把自来水煮沸五分钟、冷却后过滤，可以去除至少80%的微塑料；其效果取决于水中碳酸钙的含量，硬水效果更好。研究也有局限，只考察了三种常见塑料。这些发现为减少微塑料摄入提供了一条可能的途径；一位未参与研究的专家肯定了该研究的方法，并认为应考虑升级饮用水处理厂。

paras.en: Microplastics have become a common source of pollution across the Earth — they have settled in the deep sea and on the Himalayas, stuck inside volcanic rocks, filled the stomachs of seabirds and even fallen in fresh Antarctic snow.
paras.zh: 微塑料已成为地球上常见的污染源——它们沉积在深海和喜马拉雅山上，嵌在火山岩里，填满了海鸟的胃，甚至落在南极新下的雪中。
